source_files.module_doc:
Explicit Linux CPU pools for trusted subprocess launch threads.

A shared compute namespace (``MERLIN_COMPUTE_CPUS`` + ``MERLIN_COMPUTE_CPU_SLOTS``)
is the single limiter for every engine: one flock'd ``cpu-<n>.lock`` slot per
CPU, leased by builds, simulators, grading and preparation steps alike. It is
divided only by priority (see :func:`cpu_priority`); no CPU is reserved for a
class or an engine.

symbols.name: _explicit_priority
calls: (os.environ if environ is None else environ).get
(os.environ if environ is None else environ).get(PRIORITY_ENV, '').strip

symbols.name: lease_priority
symbols.doc:
The class this thread's next shared lease waits at.

The context's :func:`cpu_priority` wins, then the inherited process class
(``MERLIN_CPU_PRIORITY``), then :data:`GRADE`. New threads start with an
empty context, so executors that must keep a class submit through
``contextvars.copy_context().run``; otherwise they fall back to the process
class.

symbols.name: cpu_priority
symbols.doc:
Lease shared compute at ``level`` inside this context.

``export`` also publishes the class to this process environment so every
child inherits it; the environment is process-wide, so export only at a
single-purpose process entrypoint. :func:`worker_pool_command` carries a
context-only class into the workers it launches.

symbols.name: with_priority
symbols.doc: Decorator form of :func:`cpu_priority` for an entrypoint function.

symbols.name: _waiter_key
symbols.doc: ``(priority, queued_ns, pid, tid, nonce)`` for a queue entry name, else ``None``.

symbols.name: _remove_unlocked
symbols.doc: Unlink ``path`` only while it still names the inode whose lock we observed free.

symbols.name: _held_since
symbols.doc: Last heartbeat of a locked queue file; ``None`` once its owner is gone (it is then removed).

symbols.name: _live_waiter
symbols.doc: A queued owner still polling; a dead owner's entry is removed on sight.

symbols.name: _wake_local_waiters
symbols.doc:
Hand a slot freed in this process to its front waiters now; others poll.

Wake the front priority candidates without making every waiter rescan.
A deeper waiter with a disjoint roster also observes releases by polling.

symbols.name: _queued_keys
symbols.doc: Sorted keys of the live waiters in one namespace queue, shared by this process's threads.

symbols.name: _free_cpus
symbols.doc: Observe unheld slots; a shared probe never blocks a holder.

symbols.name: _waiter_roster
symbols.doc:
A bounded ticket payload, or a conservative wildcard for legacy/unknown tickets.

Filenames retain the original queue format: an old reader ignores this
payload, and an old zero-byte writer still outranks us on every free CPU.
Original writers publish the complete payload before renaming the ticket.

symbols.name: _matching
symbols.doc:
Match the earliest feasible waiters, preserving every earlier admission.

An augmenting path can move a flexible earlier waiter to another eligible
CPU so a singleton can run too. An unmatched waiter cannot use the current
free CPUs and must not reserve unrelated CPUs against later waiters.

symbols.name: _queue_assignment
symbols.doc: Match the complete queue, so a flexible head leaves singleton CPUs free.

symbols.name: _admission_holds
symbols.doc:
Freshly prove our exact acquired CPU belongs to the full queue matching.

Earlier feasible waiters remain matched first. Considering later waiters
too prevents a stale view assigning a flexible head a singleton's only CPU.
The actual acquired flock stays exclusive throughout this re-proof.

symbols.name: _Waiter
symbols.doc: One queued acquisition: a locked, uniquely named entry in the namespace queue.

symbols.name: check_compiler_cpu
symbols.doc: Reopen live CPU custody before the original broker publishes a reply.

symbols.name: current_thread_owns_cpu_lease
symbols.doc: Observe a live original slot, never a copied thread/process context.

symbols.name: CompilerCPUTransfer
symbols.doc: Private inherited FDs, never a compiler request/environment capability.

symbols.name: transfer_compiler_cpu
symbols.doc:
Transfer only this original thread's live slot to its trusted RPC child.

The caller must join/reap that child before this scope and its enclosing CPU
lease close. The token carries CPU custody only, never compiler authority.

symbols.name: borrow_compiler_cpu
symbols.doc: Activate the exact private parent slot in one trusted broker thread.

symbols.name: _acquire_slot
symbols.doc:
Take one free slot in priority order across every thread and process of the namespace.

Earlier feasible waiters (a more urgent class, or an earlier waiter of its
own class) are matched to their currently free eligible CPUs first. A
blocked waiter never reserves unrelated free CPUs. Augmenting paths keep
overlapping rosters work-conserving without displacing an earlier waiter.
FIFO within a class; no slot is held back for a class with no waiter. A
newcomer queues an entry only when it cannot take a slot at once.
``queued_since_ns`` keeps a retrying caller's place in its class.

symbols.name: selected_pool
symbols.doc:
Children inherit this thread's affinity; restore it without preexec callbacks.

An explicit slot directory grants one exclusive build per selected CPU across
threads and processes, handed out in :func:`lease_priority` order. Without it,
children may use the complete selected pool.

symbols.name: shared_compute_enabled
symbols.doc: An incomplete selection refuses instead of falling back to separate pools.

symbols.name: grading_cpus
symbols.doc: Affinity for preparation workers; acquiring a slot is the actual step owner's job.

symbols.name: compute_capacity
symbols.doc:
CPUs in the selected shared compute pool; 0 when no pool is selected.

Unset per-engine concurrency caps default to this, so the pool's slots are
the only limiter and ``MERLIN_COMPUTE_CPUS`` alone sizes every engine.

symbols.name: preparation_cpus
symbols.doc:
Affinity for unleased preparation; its bounded CPU steps lease shared slots.

Without a separate roster, preparation runs on the shared compute CPUs and
its CPU-bound steps take slots from the same pool (at :data:`PREPARATION`
when no more urgent requester owns them). An explicit roster may overlap
the pool. Preparation scopes stay unleased because they wait on children
and RPCs that acquire their own slots.

symbols.name: shared_compute_pool
symbols.doc:
Lease one compute CPU for a supervised build/simulator or bounded preparation step.

Use the same namespace across engines. Never hold a capsule/parent lease while
waiting for a child or RPC that acquires its own lease. Same-thread nested
steps reuse one lease; absent selection leaves legacy callers unchanged.
Waiters are served in :func:`lease_priority` order, FIFO within a class.

symbols.name: _carried_priority
symbols.doc: The caller's explicit lease class that a worker launched with ``env`` must carry.

symbols.name: child_environment
symbols.doc:
A copy of ``environ`` (default: this process's) carrying the caller's lease class.

Build a worker environment with this whenever it is recorded or sealed before
launch. :func:`worker_pool_command` then finds the class already present and
adds no ``env`` prefix, so the worker receives exactly the recorded mapping.
Without a shared pool or an explicit class the copy is unchanged.

symbols.name: worker_pool_command
symbols.doc:
Select unleased preparation affinity before the worker interpreter imports code.

This parent-side command owns no CPU slot: actual child step owners acquire
theirs after launch, so waiting parent workers cannot exhaust the pool. With
a shared pool, the caller's lease class travels with the worker; an ``env``
prefix supplies it when ``env`` lacks it, which changes the worker's
environment, so a caller that records ``env`` first builds it with
:func:`child_environment`.

source_files.module_doc:
Retain exact inputs and products at an actually invoked process boundary.

These observations confer no correctness or stage applicability. Callers own
which inputs/dependencies are complete and the verifier owns semantic lift.
Records are written outside invoked packages and never accepted from stdout.

symbols.name: observe_timings
symbols.doc: Collect same-context host wall intervals, without interpreting hardware costs.

symbols.name: timed_event
symbols.doc: Observe one original boundary; nested intervals must not be summed blindly.

symbols.name: timing_document
symbols.doc: No cycle, CPU-time, complete-wait or transitive-child coverage follows.

symbols.name: verify_timing_document
symbols.doc: Validate optional diagnostic intervals; file pins still own artifact custody.

symbols.name: environment_identity
symbols.doc:
Bind actual process environment bytes without retaining their values.

POSIX environment keys and values use the filesystem encoding, as Python's
process launcher does. The complete sorted mapping is hashed with lengths
and a domain separator. This is an observation, not a replay environment,
dependency closure, secret-management mechanism or sandbox qualification.

symbols.name: CallInvocation
symbols.doc: An observed Python dispatch, distinct from a subprocess command claim.

symbols.name: observe
symbols.doc: Observe only a caller's actual invocation, including failed boundaries.

symbols.name: verify
symbols.doc: Reopen exact observation bytes; completeness/applicability remain caller-owned.

symbols.name: require_environment
symbols.doc:
Reopen an actual successful process and compare its protected selection.

Older observations without this binding cannot establish environment
identity. A matching saved record alone confers no live execution authority.

symbols.name: record_artifact_reuse
symbols.doc:
Record restored bytes separately from an actual process invocation.

The live build owner must authenticate the original closed process before
calling. This byte receipt issues no runtime closure, new invocation,
compiler timing, repeat or numerical verdict.

symbols.name: verify_artifact_reuse
symbols.doc: Reopen byte provenance; saved receipts never issue a live cache owner.

source_files.module_doc:
Run a subprocess and turn a failure into the caller's own error: the helper nine modules re-wrote.

Measured 2026-09-14: baselines/{buddy,executorch,exo}, runtime/{kernel_spike,elf_audit},
runtime/backends/{spike_model,zephyr_model}, llvmlower/codegen and mining/k1 each carried a private
``_run`` doing the same thing -- stringify the argv, capture text output, raise the module's own error on
a non-zero exit with a tail of the output -- with nine different tail lengths and three different answers
to "what happens on a timeout". The error class, the tail and the timeout behaviour stay each caller's
choice; the mechanics live here once.

``wrap_timeout=False`` lets ``subprocess.TimeoutExpired`` propagate unchanged, for callers that relied on
catching it; ``True`` turns it into the caller's error with the limit that fired.

symbols.name: run_checked
symbols.doc:
Run ``cmd`` (each element ``str()``-ed), capturing text output; raise ``error`` on a non-zero exit.

The message names the exit status, the command (capped at 1000 characters) and the last ``tail``
characters of stdout and stderr. ``kw`` passes through to :func:`subprocess.run` (``cwd``, ``env``,
``input``...).

source_files.module_doc:
Typed SSA composition through existing source-checked stage compilers.

This bridge preserves tensor identities across sequential runtime launches. It
is not an arbitrary graph optimizer, a target adapter or a runtime qualifier.
Pointwise stages reuse the ordinary native compiler. Mixed stages can use the
explicit synchronous buffer runtime; no cross-stage fusion is inferred.

symbols.name: plan_connected_region
symbols.doc:
Plan one ordered same-block region, retaining every external consumer.

Source operand identity, never equal shape, connects stages. Initializers
are excluded only after native pointwise admission proves they are unread.
Unknown intervening operations refuse rather than disappearing. Inputs stay
borrowed/read-only for the full region; externally observed outputs stay live.

symbols.name: _compile_connected
symbols.doc:
Compile a connected region with source-owned bindings and explicit adapters.

``stage_options(region, stage, bindings)`` returns ordinary
``compile_source_pointwise`` options (Kernel, storage adapter, encoder, limits,
optional rewrites/pass order). It cannot replace the source, selected
contracts or bindings. All actual effects and final bytes pass native source
conformance. Inputs/outputs may reuse storage only outside their live ranges.

The explicit Continuation promises sequential completion and persistence;
qualifying it on a real runtime remains the caller's independent obligation.
Images are returned as ordered launches, not blindly concatenated binaries.

symbols.name: compile_connected_pointwise
symbols.doc: Compile source-checked finite pointwise images with retained SSA boundaries.

symbols.name: compile_connected_region
symbols.doc:
Compose native dense loops and pointwise images through explicit launches.

Target callbacks select ordinary stage compiler options. ``dense_contracts``
defaults to the common selection, or may explicitly select a different dense
engine; no target identity is inferred. Dense stages cannot consume adjacent
epilogues here: every SSA stage and visible intermediate remains independent.
Returns a ConnectedProgram whose synchronous runtime passes exact input and
output byte views to the caller's target launcher. Source is never rewritten;
refusal leaves the caller's original unfused compilation path available.

source_files.module_doc:
Synchronous execution of native mixed-region products with source-owned views.

This is generic launch/buffer composition, not target instruction lowering.
Callbacks remain responsible for target execution and completion qualification.

symbols.name: ConnectedInvocation
symbols.doc: One original SSA stage, with arguments in source operand/result order.

source_files.module_doc: Resumable source-local fusion frontiers; proposals carry no legality authority.

symbols.name: _structural_family
symbols.doc:
Small public IR observation, never a hardware eligibility decision.

Named matrix operations have declared contraction semantics. A generic is
observed as elementwise only for parallel iterators and identity maps. Signed
contractions use the existing exact scalar recurrence reader. Other forms
remain unknown; selected realization readers own storage/target proofs.

symbols.name: discover
symbols.doc:
Return a bounded page and explicit continuation, without mutating source.

Resume with ``cursor=report['next_cursor']`` and unchanged inputs. The cursor
binds exact source, capability/numeric contracts and preparation requests.
Pages report exhaustion rather than silently dropping candidates or failing
a compilation. Traversal grows one forward frontier per producer and each
shared-input prefix; it deliberately does not enumerate all graph subsets.
Row indices are stable within this bound scope, not persistent operation IDs.

source_files.module_doc:
Scheduling passes over a target's derived on-chip geometry.

Kept out of ``merlin.compile``'s flat namespace on purpose: the modules there are the machinery behind
``merlin-compile`` and every name they define is re-exported on ``merlin.compile_cli`` for callers,
which is the wrong contract for a pass whose vocabulary is deliberately generic (``Load``, ``Store``,
``Geometry``). Import from this package instead.

Exact constant-stride runs for flattened valid convolution windows.

The plan splits at output-row boundaries. Each fragment therefore has one
constant input-row stride and one contiguous destination-row interval. It does
not select a device, command encoding, capacity or profitability policy.

symbols.name: emit_convolution_gather_runs
symbols.doc:
Emit target-neutral integer index SSA using supplied arithmetic builders.

Builders supply integer ``op``, ``cmp`` and ``select`` only. Zero-length
inactive fragments may remain when a dynamic start needs fewer than the
worst-case fragment count; command consumers must guard those lengths.

symbols.name: ConvolutionResidentPanel
symbols.doc: One complete-reduction RHS panel in a caller-owned private row epoch.

symbols.name: plan_convolution_resident_panel
symbols.doc:
Maximize complete-K column residency within explicit separate stores.

One activation tile occupies rows [0,tile). RHS tiles have an injective
reduction-major layout at the opposite end. Accumulator tiles remain live
together until complete reductions store them. No operand/accumulator spill,
hardware overlap or measured profitability is inferred.

source_files.module_doc:
Order the block moves and computes of a contraction over a target's on-chip stores.

``capacity.py`` answers which tile FITS. This module answers the question after it: in what ORDER the
blocks of that tile move on chip, which of them stays resident, and where each operand's region sits --
the part a weight-stationary backend otherwise hand-writes, and the part that decides cycles.

Measured on one such backend (the capsule head-to-head experiment, whose ``STATUS.md`` carries the
Verilator and FPGA tables), four choices inside this ordering moved 1-24% of cycles on identical
instruction packing:

* loading an operand block only when its index changes, instead of once per inner step (-28% on a
  4x4-block matmul);
* issuing loads a BOUNDED number of reduction steps ahead: one step ahead beat both interleaved
  (-6%) and hoisting every load up front (which cost 7% on the same shape, because the loads crowd
  the queues ahead of the first compute);
* which operand's load is issued first inside a step;
* where the non-streamed operand's region starts: sharing a bank with the streamed operand cost
  3-15%, and the position INSIDE the other bank moved several cycles either way.

None of the four has a value that wins everywhere. The best setting depends on the shape AND on the
substrate -- one capsule reverses between a fast-memory simulator and the FPGA, where real DRAM
latency makes an earlier load pay. So they are KNOBS here, with documented defaults, never constants
compiled into a backend: a target picks values by measurement (keyed by kernel digest, the way
``perf/calibration`` keys a measured cycle count) and this pass produces the schedule for them.

Everything about the device is derived. Block edge, store rows, bank depth and the accumulator's size
come from :func:`merlin.targetgen.address_space.derive_address_space`, i.e. from that target's own RTL
facts; a quantity the facts cannot answer is a refusal (:class:`BlockScheduleError`), never a default.

This module imports nothing from merlin, so a generated backend that may not depend on merlin at run time
can VENDOR it byte for byte and run the pass itself (``tests/infra`` pins that). Deriving a
:class:`Geometry` from a target's facts is :func:`merlin.compile.scheduling.derive.geometry_from_address_space`.

Every schedule is checked before it is returned (:func:`check_residency`): a load may not overwrite a
block some later compute still expects to read. That check is what makes an aggressive knob value SAFE
to offer -- when two regions overlap, one order can be correct (the overwrite lands after the last
read) while another silently computes on the wrong bytes, and an in-order executor cannot see the
difference.

symbols.name: BlockScheduleError
symbols.doc: A schedule the target's derived facts, the program, or the knobs do not admit.

symbols.name: Geometry
symbols.doc:
The on-chip geometry a block schedule addresses, derived from one target's facts.

``block`` is the square block edge (the array edge a store row spans). ``operand_bank_rows`` is the
PER-BANK row count -- the granularity a placement policy can separate operands at -- and is ``None``
when the facts could not resolve it, which makes :data:`BANK_ALIGNED` a refusal rather than a guess.

symbols.name: Knobs
symbols.doc:
The scheduling choices, with their defaults.

Defaults are the values that measured best over the corpus this pass was lifted from, stated so a
reader knows what they are getting: load on index change, one reduction step of lookahead, the
streamed operand's load first inside a step, and the resident operand at the far end of the store.
They are a starting point for a target's own measurement, NOT a claim that they are optimal
anywhere else -- on that corpus the best value differed per shape and per substrate.

symbols.name: Contraction
symbols.doc:
One contraction to schedule: ``[m, k] x [k, n] -> [m, n]``, with the operand names a backend
resolves addresses against.

symbols.name: ConvContraction
symbols.doc:
One NHWC convolution scheduled as a contraction: each kernel tap x input-channel slice is a
reduction block, each output-channel block a resident block, each block of output pixels a streamed
block gathered tap by tap from the input feature map.

Operands, in the element coordinates :func:`execute` and a renderer address: the input as a
``[batch*in_h*in_w, ci]`` matrix, the weight as ``[kh*kw*ci, co]`` (pre-im2col layout), the output as
``[batch*out_h*out_w, co]``.

symbols.name: Load
symbols.doc:
Move one block of ``role`` from its DRAM position (in ELEMENTS) to on-chip row ``row``.

A GATHERED block (``gather`` set) is not a contiguous DRAM rectangle: on-chip row ``row + i`` is filled
from ``gather[i]``, a ``(row, col)`` element position in the operand's DRAM matrix, or from the
target's zero path when the entry is ``None`` (a convolution tap that falls outside the image). Then
``dram_row``/``dram_col`` are ``-1``, and the gather is part of the block's identity: two loads of one
block position with different gathers are different bytes.

symbols.name: GatherRun
symbols.doc:
A maximal stretch of a gather that one multi-row load can move.

``offset`` is the first gathered row, ``rows`` how many. ``source`` is the first DRAM ``(row, col)``,
and the run reads rows ``source[0] + i * row_step`` for ``i < rows`` at that column -- or ``source`` is
``None`` and every row comes from the target's zero path (``row_step`` 0). A stride-``s`` convolution
gathers every ``s``-th pixel of an image row, so its runs have ``row_step == s``.

symbols.name: gather_runs
symbols.doc:
Split a gather into the fewest runs of rows that are equally spaced in DRAM (or all zero).

A run's spacing is fixed by its first two entries and must be positive; a single entry is a run of
one. Joining the runs back, row by row, reproduces the gather exactly -- which is what lets a target
that can load several DRAM rows at a configured stride move a gather in a handful of loads instead of
one per row, without changing a single byte that reaches the chip.

symbols.name: Preload
symbols.doc:
Name the accumulator block the next :class:`Compute` writes, and (when ``weight_row`` is not
``None``) make that weight block resident first; ``None`` keeps the resident block.

symbols.name: Compute
symbols.doc: Stream ``rows`` rows from ``input_row`` through the resident weight block.

symbols.name: Store
symbols.doc: Drain one accumulator block to its DRAM position (in ELEMENTS).

symbols.name: BlockSchedule
symbols.doc: An ordered block schedule plus what produced it.

symbols.name: _regions
symbols.doc:
``(role -> (base row, rows), notes)`` for the placement policy. The streamed operand starts at
row 0; the resident operand's base is the policy's whole content.

symbols.name: check_residency
symbols.doc:
Check synchronous operand residency, accumulator ownership and output coverage.

This is the class of fault an in-order executor cannot see: it recomputes the same arithmetic on
whatever bytes are resident, so a schedule that overwrote a block too early produces numbers, not a
crash. Every read here names the block identity it expects, so an overwrite is caught structurally.
Reduction prefixes and physical accumulator rows must agree before a store.
Unknown effects or shared backings without an alias model are refused.

symbols.name: _check_reduction_lifetimes
symbols.doc:
Verify ordered, synchronous reductions and physical accumulator ownership.

This is the execution model of BlockSchedule, not a hardware completion
model. An asynchronous adapter must establish its dependencies separately.
State is proportional to represented rows and output tiles, not elements.

symbols.name: schedule_contraction
symbols.doc:
Schedule ``contraction`` on ``geometry`` under ``knobs``, or refuse.

The nest is ``knobs.loop_order`` -- reduction-major by default (step, then resident-operand block,
then streamed-operand block), which is what keeps one weight block resident across the streamed
blocks that read it. ``knobs`` decides the nest, WHERE each load is emitted relative to the computes,
and where the resident region sits; every order computes the same products, and
:func:`check_residency` refuses any that would read an overwritten block.

symbols.name: schedule_convolution
symbols.doc:
Schedule an NHWC convolution as a gathered contraction, or refuse.

Reduction blocks are ``(tap row, tap col, channel slice)`` in kernel order, each ``min(block,
ci - c0)`` channels deep; a streamed block is a block of output pixels whose rows are GATHERED, one
per pixel, from the input position that tap reads -- or from the target's zero path where the tap
falls in the padding. The gather depends on the tap and the pixel block only, never on the output
channel block, which is why ``load_on_index_change`` can load it once per ``(tap, pixel block)``
instead of once per output-channel block: the same bytes into the same rows, which
:func:`check_residency` verifies rather than assumes.

symbols.name: _schedule_nest
symbols.doc:
The one block nest both contractions share: regions, the load-due rule, the computes, the drains.

``lhs_load(mi, kk, base)`` / ``weight_load(kk, nj, base)`` build the block moves; the three extents
are ``(K, N, M)`` block counts; ``k_depth`` / ``m_rows`` / ``n_cols`` give a block's edge along each
axis, so partial edge blocks need no special case here.

symbols.name: _schedule_ops
symbols.doc: Build one panel, continuing global K and storing only at the final reduction.

symbols.name: ConvolutionPanel
symbols.doc:
Operation range after which operand rows may be reused.

Accumulators stay live across K panels until the final K panel stores them.
This logical boundary supplies no target fence or asynchronous completion.

symbols.name: schedule_tiled_convolution
symbols.doc:
Keep output panels live while streaming bounded, reusable reduction panels.

This target-independent family preserves NHWC gathers, tails and original
tap/channel reduction order. Operand rows are reused between K panels; live
output rows are reused only after stores. Candidates minimize requested
operand ELEMENTS (including padding zeros), not bytes, traffic or cycles.
For each M/N candidate, the largest fitting K panel minimizes panel count.
Bias, output conversion and physical completion stay with the caller. A
target must establish exact continuation and completion before consumption.
This finite schedule is bounded before expansion; it emits no hardware loop.

symbols.name: execute
symbols.doc:
Run ``schedule`` on host arrays exactly as an in-order device would, and return the output.

The schedule's own oracle: every row a load writes, every block a preload makes resident, every
accumulate and every drain is simulated at the addresses the schedule names -- nothing is recomputed
from the contraction. So a schedule that addresses the wrong rows, drains the wrong accumulator block
or reuses a stale resident block produces a wrong ``out``, which a direct ``lhs @ weight`` exposes in
milliseconds, before any backend or simulator is involved.

symbols.name: _ordered
symbols.doc: The loads of one emission group, ordered by ``load_grouping`` (stable within a role).

symbols.name: _emit
symbols.doc:
Place each group's loads relative to the computes, per ``lookahead_steps``.

At depth 0 the emission group is one iteration of the two outer loops, and a load sits in its nest
position -- immediately before the compute that first needs it -- or, under ``ROLE`` grouping, with
the group's other loads ahead of its computes. At depth ``d`` the group is a whole outer step, issued
``d`` steps early. At ``None`` every load is hoisted ahead of every compute, and the whole prologue is
one group.

symbols.name: schedule_interface_program
symbols.doc:
Schedule every resident matmul an interface program commits, and every convolution, in program
order.

``tensors`` maps a name to that tensor's spec (anything with ``shape``, or a mapping carrying
``"shape"``); ``commands`` is the program's command list. Any other command -- a convolution, a
movement, an epilogue this pass does not model -- is a refusal, so a caller never receives a
schedule that silently dropped work.

symbols.name: _conv_command
symbols.doc: One ``CONV2D`` command as a :class:`ConvContraction`, refusing what the nest cannot express.

source_files.module_doc:
Compress finite affine primitive-call streams into checked ordinary host loops.

This changes static representation only. Every dynamic call, operand and its
order must match the original finite stream. No target effects, hardware loop
instructions or latency are inferred. Unsupported annotated calls remain literal.

symbols.name: _preflight
symbols.doc: Bound traversal before invoking the ordinary recursive IR checkers.

symbols.name: verify_command_compaction
symbols.doc:
Compare actual loop execution to the complete original primitive sequence.

The verifier uses the existing index evaluator and signed intermediate
checker, not a retained pattern, hash-only assertion or optimizer replay.
Verification allocates no dynamic trace beyond the original finite input.

symbols.name: compact_command_stream
symbols.doc:
Infer repeated affine call blocks under explicit search and code budgets.

The source is finite. Calls with dependencies/configuration annotations,
pointers, floating operands or nonliteral operands remain unchanged. This
pass neither removes setup nor changes the dynamic instruction count.
A Phase 2 consumer may select this after checked scheduling, then use the
ordinary counted-loop emitter and its original executable-size admission.

source_files.module_doc:
Compact rectangular dense schedules in the existing counted-loop kernel IR.

Merlin owns panel blocking, retention, tails and source reduction order. An
explicit adapter translates typed moves/computes and projects their *actual*
operands back. Instruction implementation and physical row mapping remain OOT.
No target lookup, opaque output inference, or latency model is used here.

symbols.name: DenseMemoryView
symbols.doc:
Assigned rows in an explicitly identified physical backing.

``base``/``capacity``/``alignment`` are in this view's row units. Different
row widths may alias a backing only through their explicit byte mapping.
These are usable assignments after packing/DMA/other reservations.

symbols.name: DenseLoopAdapter
symbols.doc:
Public instruction boundary. Neither function is selected by its name.

Projection must decode the actual call operands, not retained requests.
The declaration is conditional on the adapter's independent qualification;
synthetic adapters establish only the shared algorithm's scope.

symbols.name: emit_compact_dense
symbols.doc:
Emit bounded panel nests without enumerating tensor elements or tiles.

The supported family starts a zero-initialized reduction on its first
compute and keeps each output accumulator through the complete K domain.
Bias/other seeds retain their original route until explicitly implemented.

symbols.name: schedule_compact_dense
symbols.doc:
Ordinary scheduling entry: choose, emit and independently verify output.

No candidate preserves the caller's existing legal route. A checking-budget
refusal may try one simple streaming loop; every address and dependency is
rechecked. A concrete invariant failure never triggers fallback. The explicit
disjointness premise belongs to the original source/runtime boundary, not
to an optimization candidate. Missing decoder/completion facts diagnose.
With selected contracts, geometry, formats and assigned windows are checked
against both pinned documents; resources=None derives available budgets.
Reservations name canonical backing bytes after upstream allocation.

source_files.module_doc:
Full-K shared-LHS groups using the existing dense blocks and counted loops.

This conditional original-host entry needs independently qualified retention,
interleaving and explicit pointer transport. Missing capabilities retain the
original separate contraction route. It issues no target or Phase 2 grants.

symbols.name: implementation_paths
symbols.doc: Direct implementation plus the unchanged original scheduling library.

symbols.name: emit_compact_dense_group
symbols.doc: One M outer nest, one LHS load panel, then complete ordered members.

symbols.name: schedule_compact_dense_group
symbols.doc:
Choose and check one bounded full-K group before actual emission.

Distinct RHS/accumulator assigned windows and complete explicit external
pointers are required. A declaration or this result alone grants no effect
permission. Missing retention/full-K capacity yields no candidate.

source_files.module_doc:
Check actual full-K shared-LHS groups through physical noninterference.

Every member has separate RHS and accumulator windows. Only after checking all
actual role footprints and external pointer bindings may the existing compact
checker project a member view. These proof views neither reset machine memory
nor execute a member separately. Original qualification remains required.

symbols.name: DenseLHSReuseLaw
symbols.doc:
Original implementation premises; constructing this data grants nothing.

The original qualifier covers the full admitted operand/selector domain,
including every RHS load, preload, compute, store and implicit/configuration
effect, independent-member interleaving, and omitted-load fault/observation
effects. RTL capacity and a syntactic pointer do not establish these laws.

symbols.name: _range
symbols.doc: Conservative bounds over the existing integer/select expression language.

symbols.name: verify_compact_dense_group
symbols.doc: Reconstruct all actual member effects, coverage, retention and final outputs.

source_files.module_doc:
Symbolic checks over projected *actual* counted-loop dense instructions.

Coverage is proved by bounded domains, exact cardinality and injectivity.
Residency is a latest-write condition over physical byte intervals and program
order. No loop is expanded and no tensor is allocated by this checker.
Completion is synchronous in this family; asynchronous adapters must not use it.

symbols.name: DenseVerificationUnavailable
symbols.doc: The selected checking tool or budget could not establish the result.

symbols.name: _requested_elements
symbols.doc:
Sum piecewise-constant extents without visiting dynamic instances.

The supported dimension language is constants and finite equality selects.
Addresses retain the full affine language. Unknown dimension forms decline
this accounting instead of substituting a plan's traffic estimate.

symbols.name: verify_compact_dense
symbols.doc:
Verify current loop bounds, tails, source addresses and physical lifetimes.

The projection adapter remains responsible for independently qualified
instruction semantics. This result is not a final machine-emission receipt.

source_files.module_doc:
Remove redundant setup using independently decoded persistent state effects.

This extends the schedule IR's sets/assumes vocabulary with the missing
execution contract: actual operand decoding, clobbers, ordering and a qualified
pure idempotent write. An annotation or matching instruction name alone never
authorizes deleting an instruction. Unknown effects retain the instruction and
forget all known state. Initial state is unknown for each invocation.

symbols.name: ConfigurationUnavailable
symbols.doc: The selected configuration family cannot establish a legal rewrite.

symbols.name: ConfigurationEffects
symbols.doc:
Actual integer-valued configuration fields, in instruction order.

ordered requires independently qualified visibility in program order.
pure_write means ONLY persistent, idempotent register writes: no enqueue,
pulse, acknowledgement, memory, status, synchronization or other effect.
Reads precede clobbers and writes. Missing ordering forgets all state.

symbols.name: eliminate_redundant_configuration
symbols.doc:
Keep the first write and drop only fully redundant pure later writes.

No dead-store motion, partial instruction rewrite, loop unrolling or
cross-invocation state assumption. Unknown ordering/effects are barriers.

symbols.name: verify_configuration_rewrite
symbols.doc: Reconstruct legal omissions from actual output, without a selected plan.

symbols.name: verify_configuration_state
symbols.doc:
Require actual uses to have established values after every later rewrite.

Fusion, allocation and inserted spills can change configuration effects.
Unknown instructions clear state; a later required read needs a new setter.
This check does not assume that an exact memory copy preserves registers.

source_files.module_doc:
Persistent configuration cleanup on actual, declared instruction MLIR.

The existing schedule algorithm owns deletion legality. This adapter reads the
selected generated ISA schema, preserves every other SSA operation and checks
the realized IR independently. It interprets neither opaque backend artifacts
nor target instruction names. Execution qualification is an original caller
premise, separate from structural facts, declarations and these checks.

symbols.name: ConfigurationIRSelection
symbols.doc:
Original-owned input; a qualification identifier does not establish support.

Missing qualification, unavailable effects or exceeded analysis budgets
retain unchanged IR. The caller freezes this object before invoking a
compiler package and separately qualifies its instruction implementation.

symbols.name: _scope
symbols.doc: Opaque region semantics do not establish sequential block execution.

symbols.name: _opaque
symbols.doc: Preserve unknown nested SSA exactly, including types omitted by structural equivalence.

symbols.name: verify_configuration_ir
symbols.doc: Check actual omissions and every retained SSA operation, not a chosen plan.

source_files.module_doc:
Hoist loop-invariant persistent setup using qualified actual call effects.

Only an ordered pure-write prefix moves, immediately before a nonempty loop.
Every remaining call must have known ordered effects and preserve those fields.
The verifier independently matches actual moved calls and their complete scope;
no instruction name, geometry, latency or initial register value is assumed.

symbols.name: verify_loop_configuration_rewrite
symbols.doc:
Check actual loop prefixes, field invariance and every retained instruction.

This accepts only prefix motion, with identical loop extents, operands,
annotations and non-configuration call order. It does not replay the
optimizer or accept its selected moves as evidence.

symbols.name: hoist_loop_configuration
symbols.doc: Move complete legal setup prefixes; unknown effects retain their original scope.

source_files.module_doc: Bound live spatial/output-channel tiles around a complete resident RHS panel.

symbols.name: plan_convolution_output_group
symbols.doc:
Select a bounded M group without spilling full-K live accumulators.

The static unroll bound is explicit and limits code expansion; capacity
chooses the remaining extent. Profitability and target weight reuse remain
separate choices. Each K epoch loads all LHS tiles before immutable reads;
the caller must complete every read before the next epoch overwrites them.

source_files.module_doc:
Bounded adjacent synchronous copy proposals under an original merge law.

No target opcode, request limit, fault behavior or observational equivalence is
inferred. Final encoded-program admission remains the original caller's job.

symbols.name: coalesce_private_copies
symbols.doc:
Combine adjacent compatible requests; missing information retains source.

Existing initialization/ownership admission is intentionally unchanged.
Virtual-only addresses, differently qualified forms, partial initialization
across objects and unmodeled external aliases remain outside this family.

source_files.module_doc:
Check actual adjacent-copy effects under a separate original merge law.

Exact-copy effects alone do not authorize combining requests. The caller must
independently qualify the count/alignment envelope and absence of faults or
other program-visible observations. This first family retains existing private
initialization rules and never infers a target's DMA semantics.

symbols.name: verify_coalesced_copies
symbols.doc:
Reconstruct contiguous groups from actual effects, never a proposed plan.

Unchanged calls remain byte-for-byte IR equal and in their original order.
Every changed instruction must cover two or more immediately consecutive
original exact copies, including all source/destination bytes and semantics.

source_files.module_doc:
Forward private exact copies through physically shared addressable views.

The source must stay unchanged until the destination's last read. Both views
must address the same physical backing; no cross-space handoff, conversion,
asynchronous completion or in-place arithmetic capability is inferred.

symbols.name: eliminate_private_copies
symbols.doc:
Produce a bounded candidate; allocation and independent checking follow.

A complete private destination is initialized by one synchronous exact
copy, then only read. Forward those reads to the original byte interval
when no intervening write can change it. Other consumers remain ordered.
Unknown effects are handled by the ordinary storage admission barrier.

source_files.module_doc:
Pipeline qualified input copies into existing private buffer slots.

This extends the single-outstanding-copy family without widening its admission.
Concurrent copies and launch motion across pure token waits need a separate
original-owner qualification. Capacity alone grants neither. Launch order,
waits, arithmetic, descriptors and setup remain intact; no fence is removed.

symbols.name: CopyPipelineAdmission
symbols.doc:
Selected software overlap semantics with fact-derived queue bounds.

crossing_pairs qualify a launch across a synchronous memory-only operation
or a pure token-completion wait. concurrent_pairs qualify simultaneously
pending external-to-private exact copies, in their preserved issue order.
Both require disjoint memory effects, including aliases of the same bank.
Qualification must cover shared ports, configuration and descriptor state;
these pairs are never inferred from storage capacity or instruction names.

symbols.name: resolve_copy_pipeline_admission
symbols.doc:
Resolve a separately reviewed software contract against selected RTL facts.

This resolver supplies no qualification or candidate access grant. The
original execution owner must qualify the exact selected overlap semantics
and bind the actual hardware revision, as for StorageAdapter itself.
Missing/UNKNOWN capacity refuses rather than guessing a queue depth.

symbols.name: CopyPipelinePolicy
symbols.doc: Finite search choices, independently capped by the selected admission.

symbols.name: _resource_trace
symbols.doc: Check actual completion/alias hazards, pending-copy pairs and occupancy.

symbols.name: verify_copy_pipeline
symbols.doc:
Check actual instructions, every inverted dependence and resource trace.

This does not trust a greedy search, proposed buffer plan or move report.
It also does not establish that emitted target code has these effects:
final decoding/binding remains the original target execution owner's job.

symbols.name: pipeline_private_copies
symbols.doc:
Hoist existing input-copy launches into qualified fixed private slots.

A two-slot source and max_pending_copies=2 permit bounded double buffering;
no storage, async instruction or wait is invented. Unknown state, missing
pair qualification and capacity exhaustion stop motion conservatively.

symbols.name: _CopyPipelineOwner
symbols.doc: Original admission and implementation, never restored from a record.

symbols.name: copy_pipeline_motion
symbols.doc:
Bind one original qualified copy pass to the ordinary fixed storage stage.

This V8 companion adds no import permission to historical SDK inventories.
Unknown admission leaves the exact original compilation path available.

source_files.module_doc:
Check omitted payload writes under an original qualified deletion law.

This is an already-placed, invocation-private storage proof. It supplies no
instruction, fault, observation, ownership, completion or target qualification.

symbols.name: WriteDeletionLaw
verify_dead_writes
symbols.doc:
Read actual omissions and prove every changed byte killed before reading.

All surviving calls must be unchanged and ordered. Reads precede writes
within each operation, including implicit/RMW reads. Alias views share the
original physical backing coordinates. Final private differences also refuse.

source_files.module_doc:
Original-host DSE selection for one ordinary schedule compilation.

This companion is outside frozen SDK inventories. Its factory binds a live
original deletion law and verification code; serialized records create no
qualification and author requests cannot choose its callbacks or premises.

symbols.name: compile_schedule_with_dead_writes
symbols.doc:
Compile ONCE through the ordinary pre-emission pipeline.

Missing law preserves the original default route. The original host owns
the live law/verifier selection; records or callback names grant nothing.

source_files.module_doc: Bounded dead private-payload proposals; original delete permission required.

symbols.name: eliminate_dead_writes
symbols.doc:
Remove only complete admitted payloads killed before any observation.

The candidate never changes addresses, order, ownership or allocation.
Unknown/async effects and unavailable proof retain the original program.

source_files.module_doc:
Fact-bound admission for the existing compact dense scheduling family.

RTL references constrain geometry and physical windows. Software declares
ordered modular arithmetic, effects and execution. Assigned windows come from
allocation; this module never treats a whole memory as free scratch space.

symbols.name: dense_contract_draft
symbols.doc:
Editable shape of the existing resolver, with every target assertion unknown.

Supported family assumptions are exposed separately as DENSE_SEMANTICS; they
are not inferred target properties. No instruction, geometry, allocation,
policy, completion behavior or qualification is selected by this template.

symbols.name: DenseSchedulingUnavailable
symbols.doc: Declared capabilities cannot implement this family; retain a legal source route.

symbols.name: DenseLogicalPointerABI
symbols.doc:
Declared logical pointer access, separate from physical tile storage.

These software declarations do not qualify an implementation. Original
independent format/effect qualification remains a separate caller input.

symbols.name: DenseIntegerReadout
symbols.doc: One declared unary integer output path; qualification is separate.

symbols.name: resolve_dense_contract
symbols.doc: Read only the explicit versioned dense extension, never infer semantics.

source_files.module_doc:
Bank-separated private full-K operand caching for a dense contraction.

The target owns physical addresses, encodings and completion. This planner
assigns enough rows for one all-K LHS tile and a capacity-bounded RHS column
panel. No overlap or measured service capability is inferred from capacity.

symbols.name: plan_dense_resident_panel
symbols.doc: Maximize a complete-K RHS panel after reserving disjoint LHS banks.

symbols.name: plan_dense_stationary_panel
symbols.doc:
Balance complete-K row groups and column panels under private capacity.

Requested DRAM bytes order proposals, followed by stationary-weight fills.
These are compiler heuristics, not timing observations or fitness claims.

symbols.name: plan_dense_output_panel
symbols.doc:
Cache full-K operands and distinct full-reduction output columns.

The target supplies the accumulator capacity and readout mapping. Each
column block owns one accumulator block until the final readout fence.

symbols.name: plan_dense_joint_panel
symbols.doc:
Reuse row groups and full-K column panels with every output live.

Total input bytes order candidates, then stationary-weight fills. The
simultaneous M*N block product must fit private accumulator capacity.
This heuristic grants no timing or overlap authority.

source_files.module_doc:
Capacity planning for a private dense product with a complete resident RHS.

The target supplies its row geometry and a disjoint LHS staging reservation.
This plan supplies no synchronization, instruction semantics or overlap claim.

symbols.name: plan_dense_rhs_residency
symbols.doc:
Plan only disjoint full-RHS storage and one complete output accumulator.

Decline before emission if the padded matrix, bounded static preparation or
private LHS/output tile does not fit. The caller must own the complete local
storage epoch and retain ordinary external-buffer alias/lifetime checks.

source_files.module_doc:
Bind typed source matmul semantics to the existing compact dense scheduler.

Targets still supply physical storage assignments and qualified instruction
adapters. Merlin derives the problem from current source, verifies the scalar
recurrence and initialization, and retains source custody through C emission.

symbols.name: DenseSourceUnavailable
symbols.doc: Unsupported source semantics; a caller may retain its existing legal route.

symbols.name: read_zero_seeded_integer_matmul
symbols.doc: Read tensor semantics and geometry without selecting hardware or a schedule.

symbols.name: read_dense_source
symbols.doc:
Match current exact signed dense source before asking a target for policy.

This establishes neither runtime ownership nor executable target support.
Compilation repeats admission and binds the complete original module.

symbols.name: read_source_dense
symbols.doc:
Read supported scalar semantics without starting a scheduling session.

This uses the same source admission as compilation. A model discovery pass
can decline unrelated operations before verifying or scheduling the complete
module; compilation independently repeats admission on the current source.

symbols.name: schedule_source_dense
symbols.doc:
Compile one current source operation; missing capability keeps fallback explicit.

No shape, model name or provenance label selects the transformation. The
scalar recurrence, source extents, zero initialization and selected formats
must agree. Physical/runtime disjointness is an original-caller premise,
never inferred from different tensor SSA names. Returns None only when the
existing bounded scheduler cannot realize a legal candidate.
``pass_order`` selects source stages; ``schedule_pass_order`` reaches the
compact scheduler's independent prerequisite and realization checks.

symbols.name: read_source_dense_readout
symbols.doc: Match one original unary output computation to its selected exact readout.

symbols.name: read_source_dense_readout_chain
symbols.doc:
Compose complete unary integer stages and match the original physical recipe.

Each source stage retains its exact typed casts, clamps and arithmetic.
No intermediate may have another observer. This checks correspondence to
a separately selected readout, not equivalence under reassociation or an
approximate conversion. Runtime captures, broadcasts and unknown effects
preserve the original dense-plus-source route.

source_files.module_doc:
Derive a block-schedule :class:`~merlin.compile.scheduling.block_schedule.Geometry` from a target's facts.

Kept apart from ``block_schedule.py`` so that module imports nothing from merlin and a generated backend
can vendor it verbatim; this is the one place the pass meets :mod:`merlin.targetgen.address_space`.

symbols.name: geometry_from_machine
symbols.doc:
Project a :class:`~merlin.sched.mach.Machine` onto the vendorable :class:`Geometry`, or refuse.

The projection runs ONE WAY, and deliberately. ``block_schedule.py`` imports nothing from merlin so
a generated backend can vendor it byte for byte; a ``Geometry`` that reached back into the machine
model would make every minted package depend on merlin at run time, which the package integrity scan
rejects. So the machine is the richer description and this is a lossy read of it.

What the projection DROPS, said plainly so nothing degrades silently: ports, arbiter, sharing, the
unit set, the thread hierarchy, per-instruction cost, and every :class:`Unknown` the machine carries.
A block schedule that needs any of those needs a second projection, not a wider ``Geometry``.

symbols.name: geometry_from_address_space
symbols.doc:
Derive from :class:`~merlin.targetgen.address_space.AddressSpace`, or refuse.

Refuses rather than defaults on: no array geometry, a non-square array (this weight-stationary
model has one square block edge, and which edge a rectangular array's block spans is a choice
no fact here makes), a missing operand or accumulator store, and a store whose row count the
facts could not derive. Stores are resolved to their roles by ROW WIDTH
(:func:`~merlin.targetgen.address_space.operand_store`,
:func:`~merlin.targetgen.address_space.accumulator_store`), never by the name an extractor
happened to give them, and a refusal quotes the resolver's reason.

source_files.module_doc:
Bounded exact device spills through the ordinary temporary allocation entry.

Only explicitly selected device register classes participate. Every insertion
reprojects actual instructions and recomputes liveness, physical allocation and
completion checks. Unknown costs use a deterministic longest-unused-gap policy;
no cycle model or host CPU register allocator is supplied.

symbols.name: allocate_with_spills
symbols.doc:
Try legal placement, then bounded exact spill/reload insertion and replan.

None preserves the caller's legal fallback when this bounded family cannot
fit. A failed invariant or unavailable checker is never treated as evidence
that another unchecked candidate is legal.

source_files.module_doc:
Read a closed typed signed-dot proposal and positional pointer declaration.

This public compiler helper checks current source against supplied analysis data.
That data is not an original proof receipt. It grants no numerical, execution,
source-owner, storage-lifetime or timing authority; independent host checkers
still establish every corresponding obligation on the actual emitted program.
Only standard tensor/arithmetic/function/linalg grammar is loaded.

Bounded straight-line configuration/barrier proposals; no execution authority.

Target adapters supply exact effects. Unknown operations forget configuration
and require a later barrier. A retained configuration command is itself pending
work: only adjacent barriers, or barriers made adjacent by a redundant write,
can disappear. This module is standalone for byte-identical candidate vendoring.

symbols.name: cleanup_indices
symbols.doc: Return retained original indices; never move, insert or modify work.

symbols.name: verify_cleanup
symbols.doc: Independently prove omissions against actual retained ordered effects.

source_files.module_doc: Export canonical shared compiler sources for explicit host review.

symbols.name: export_shared_scheduling
symbols.doc:
Write one declared source set, without granting candidate import access.

The host must review the members and separately select its existing
CompilerLibraryContract. No target, provider, grader, reference output or
calibration record is discovered or included. Namespace glue is the only
source replacement; every algorithm/checker file is copied byte for byte.

symbols.name: export_dense_planner
symbols.doc: Write exact public sources and return identities for the complete release.

source_files.module_doc:
Consume one qualified physical composition and verify its actual arithmetic.

Only adjacent, synchronous elementwise operations with a private, unobserved
intermediate are composed. Single-readout admission reuses the existing public
capability vocabulary. Instruction encoding and physical view selection remain
target-owned; Merlin reconstructs the returned call's numerical and memory
effects before allocation, then the ordinary pipeline checks the final bytes.

symbols.name: verify_fusion_step
symbols.doc: Find the realized collapsed pair; accept no selected pair or arithmetic plan.

symbols.name: plan_fusion
symbols.doc: Build and check actual target calls; allocation can still select fallback.

source_files.module_doc:
Select exact physical fusion from pinned software semantics and RTL bounds.

Reuse the existing scalar MLIR correspondence and physical fusion planner.
Target callbacks emit instructions; selected declarations bind the operation,
layout and resource domain. Neither source text nor an identity qualifies it.

symbols.name: resolve_fusion_contract
symbols.doc: Resolve only explicit typed semantics, physical routes and structural bounds.

source_files.module_doc:
Typed scalar MLIR correspondence for exact elementwise composition.

This is an immutable verification DAG, not another arithmetic language. The
operation meanings and widths remain those of the actual scalar MLIR. Only
total integer operations are admitted; no reassociation, approximation or
floating-environment policy is inferred from a target capability.

symbols.name: UnsupportedElementwise
symbols.doc: Keep the original operation: its scalar semantics are outside this family.

symbols.name: ScalarBudgetExceeded
symbols.doc: A candidate exceeds a selected compile-time bound; retain its source.

symbols.name: ElementwiseSemantics
symbols.doc:
Qualified contiguous elementwise execution with ordinary byte memory.

Every read access is one function argument, in access order; the sole final
write is the scalar return. Every access has exactly `elements` values.
All arguments of an element are read before writing that element. There
are no hidden effects, volatile accesses, state, traps or cross-element
dependencies. Exact in-place aliases are allowed; shifted aliases are not.
These execution properties require independent adapter qualification.

symbols.name: scalar_graph
symbols.doc: Reopen actual scalar IR; cache only an immutable, byte-bound typed DAG.

source_files.module_doc:
Explicit shared compiler source owners; no discovery or import grants.

The export writer and ordinary pass receipts consume this same roster. Adding
an owner requires review of its import/resource closure and authoring boundary.
This roster does not attest loaded code or external dependency implementations.

symbols.name: library_modules
symbols.doc: Select a closed reviewed inventory; this grants no import access.

symbols.name: shared_library_sources
symbols.doc: Current source identities, equal for every treatment of one library.

source_files.module_doc:
Emit checked counted-loop index programs through a caller's LLVM builder.

The target callback lowers each actual instruction and owns its effects. This
bridge supplies host loops and integer address expressions only; completion
annotations must never disappear during emission.

symbols.name: FnBuilderIndexAdapter
symbols.doc:
Adapt Merlin's ordinary LLVM FnBuilder without reconstructing a schedule.

Only signed i64 host indices and ascending, positive-step loops are admitted.
The target callback still implements actual instructions and their completion.
This adapter does not infer target semantics or erase execution annotations.

source_files.module_doc:
Original-qualified connected pointwise composition with two live outputs.

One existing instruction kernel, allocator and emission pipeline are reused.
This original-host entry grants neither device capabilities nor author access.
Missing composition support retains the caller's original individual route.

symbols.name: read_source_multioutput
symbols.doc:
Read an exact adjacent fan-out, preserving every external observer.

P must have exactly its two epilogue users and no publication or escape.
Consumer results remain the original ordered outputs. No source is cloned
or mutated and no instruction/physical execution permission is inferred.

symbols.name: implementation_paths
symbols.doc: Direct owners plus the already reviewed shared scheduling source roster.

symbols.name: compile_source_multioutput
symbols.doc:
Check one composed program before allocation and after actual byte decode.

The original live caller supplies every semantic/effect implementation.
The existing scheduler owns allocation, repair, limits and final emission;
this entry cannot manufacture a missing physical composition capability.

source_files.module_doc:
Reconstruct one private producer and both actual physical consumers.

This checks an original-qualified composition, not a capability declaration.
Every instruction still has the existing single-result scalar/effect semantics.
The shared producer's physical byte generation, work and every output are
checked together before any final-output projection.

symbols.name: MultiOutputCompositionLaw
symbols.doc:
Original execution/removal premises for a closed instruction composition.

Identifiers do not establish these premises. The original caller selects
qualified implementations and exact decoded instruction/semantic-key roles.
The checker separately proves physical retention and source correspondence.

symbols.name: verify_multioutput_fusion
symbols.doc:
Read the actual whole instruction program, never a claimed fusion plan.

The first domain uses synchronous single-result arithmetic, private P and
direct final epilogue writes. Exact input-staging copies may have explicit
waits. P cannot migrate to a copied backing between its two consumers.

source_files.module_doc:
Checked affine-to-panel packing and rectangular transfer aggregation.

The source is an explicit immutable affine matrix view. Storage is an assigned
invocation-private byte window, after reservations. Panel sizes are choices;
transfer widths, strides and alignment are selected capabilities, never facts
inferred from a compute tile. This module supplies no physical instruction,
completion, ownership qualification or asynchronous overlap authority.

symbols.name: AffineMatrixSource
symbols.doc:
A read-only matrix view, with all addresses and strides measured in bytes.

Zero strides represent broadcast reads. A transposed view is supported by
exchanging its row/column strides. Negative strides retain another route.
The bounding allocation is distinct from the logical view's first byte.

symbols.name: PanelTransferLimits
symbols.doc:
Selected synchronous rectangular copy/zero capabilities in byte units.

Every transferred row must satisfy address and length alignment. A stride
limit of zero admits no multi-row operation of that kind. A single-row
operation has no stride requirement. Zero fill means exact byte zeros.
These declarations must be bound to actual instruction semantics by the
target consumer; they are not extracted from a preferred schedule.

symbols.name: resolve_panel_transfer_limits
symbols.doc:
Resolve a versioned software contract's explicit numeric RTL references.

Every bound/alignment comes from its selected fact path, including zero
stride bounds that disable multi-row transfers. Software declares exact
copy, zero-fill and completion semantics separately. Neither these values
nor a declaration establish actual instruction or execution qualification.
No compute dimension, memory width or default supplies a missing bound.

symbols.name: PackedPanelLayout
symbols.doc:
Panel-major storage, with rows shared by adjacent primitive column tiles.

The layout covers a whole logical matrix. Panel tails and row-alignment
gaps contain zeros. A compute consumer must separately prove that its
addressing can read the tile subviews returned by ``tile_first_byte``.
Storage capacity alone does not establish that addressing capability.

symbols.name: check_panel_transfers
symbols.doc:
Check actual rectangles against the independent affine byte mapping.

Each actual destination row is checked against the matrix coordinates of
its physical panel row; no retained planner request is trusted. Sorted
intervals prove exact coverage once, including zero tails/alignment gaps.
The budget counts rectangle rows, not tensor elements or payload values.

symbols.name: _rectangles
symbols.doc: Join disjoint row segments only when their actual address steps agree.

symbols.name: plan_packed_panels
symbols.doc:
Pack adjacent compute tiles into checked wide transfer panels.

``panel_tiles`` is an explicit optimization choice. Source scalar reads
become wide copies only when its affine column stride proves contiguity.
Both exact tails and alignment gaps are initialized without over-reading.
Unknown/unaligned copies refuse instead of reading neighbouring bytes.

symbols.name: execute_panel_transfers

source_files.module_doc:
Bounded iteration checking for counted, independently drained memory blocks.

This checks every dynamic block, not a sampled prefix or affine recurrence. It
preserves counted IR for emission and establishes only the explicitly projected
memory/completion obligations. It supplies no instruction semantics or schedule.

symbols.name: resolve_drained_period_admission
symbols.doc: Resolve explicit assumptions, not a certificate or target qualification.

symbols.name: check_drained_period
symbols.doc:
Check every bounded iteration, retaining the caller's ordinary route on refusal.

Each iteration must independently initialize its complete private objects and
drain all actual asynchronous commands. There is no carried pending work or
private live-in state. Tails are checked exactly if expressible under those
same requirements; partial initialization and unbounded domains refuse.

source_files.module_doc:
Check source pointwise arithmetic through allocation, fusion and encoding.

Targets supply the original instruction sequence and qualified implementations.
Merlin reads current typed source, checks that sequence, runs the existing
scheduler, then independently reconstructs the final bytes' scalar dataflow.
This bounded family admits contiguous integer vector fragments, not opaque
backend output, floating reassociation, broadcasts or asynchronous arithmetic.

symbols.name: PointwiseScheduleCandidate
symbols.doc: A proposed instruction program and its exact private storage declarations.

symbols.name: PointwiseRewriteContext
symbols.doc:
Current computation and selected resource data available to a new pass.

No checker, evaluator or reference answer is supplied. The original caller
still owns the candidate source revision and execution sandbox.

symbols.name: PointwiseScheduleRewrite
symbols.doc:
Author-supplied transformation; its output receives no proof authority.

New implementations may change actual instructions and private temporaries,
beyond the built-in scheduling knobs. Only the bounded synchronous integer
source family and independently selected capabilities below are supported.

symbols.name: _configuration_writes
symbols.doc:
Separate persistent writes from already source-checked scalar reads.

Pure writes can be omitted only by the existing independent state induction.
Other state mutation, unknown visibility and pulses remain unsupported.
Full programs separately prove every arithmetic read's established settings.

symbols.name: read_pointwise_source
symbols.doc: Retain every typed scalar operation, constant and conversion in order.

symbols.name: PointwiseBindings
symbols.doc:
Original runtime's contiguous tensor bindings, in source operand order.

Distinct external spaces must be physically disjoint, as selected storage
declares. Exact same-window input aliases are allowed; shifted aliases and
input/output overlap are refused. This premise needs runtime qualification,
not deduction from different tensor SSA names. Byte order is explicit for
every input followed by the result. All buffers are borrowed for one call.

symbols.name: _verify_vectors
symbols.doc:
Check every output fragment against its original logical source interval.

Copies preserve byte provenance. Original inputs can be sliced on element
boundaries; computed fragments must be read completely. No expression
slicing or per-element expansion is needed to verify tiled arithmetic.

symbols.name: compile_source_pointwise
symbols.doc:
Use the ordinary scheduler with source admission and final-byte checking.

UnsupportedElementwise leaves the caller's original source route available.
An incorrect provider sequence raises ValueError before any result escapes.
This entry neither invents instruction selection nor qualifies execution.
Optional new rewrite implementations must pass the same source, resource,
configuration and final-byte checks as existing transformations. At most
eight uniquely named rewrites run, with fixed per-program work ceilings.
Rewrite tuple order is candidate policy. ``pass_order`` selects source
stages; ``schedule_pass_order`` selects the checked inner schedule stages.

source_files.module_doc:
Bind final encoded-program checks to selected structural and software facts.

The existing finalizer owns counting and safe segmentation. This module binds
its limits and reconstructs effects from actual fixed-width ISA words, rather
than trusting a provider's request stream. Qualification of the instruction
implementation and launch persistence remains a separate runtime obligation.

Final encoded-program checks and conservative continuation-safe segmentation.

Instruction decoding, instruction semantics and launch implementation belong to
the selected target. The shared algorithm never guesses a word width, branch
reach, address window, completion rule or preserved resource. Every check reads
the final bytes through that explicitly qualified decoder.

symbols.name: EncodedAccess
symbols.doc: An exact byte interval read or written by one decoded instruction.

symbols.name: Continuation
symbols.doc:
Selected launch contract, independent of an optimization candidate.

Launches execute sequentially, begin at offset zero and establish completion
and visibility before the following launch. Only named spaces persist.
This declaration needs separate target/runtime execution qualification.

symbols.name: _pending_after
symbols.doc: May-pending completion over actual branches, without executing loop trips.

symbols.name: finalize_program
symbols.doc:
Count/check actual final instructions, then slice only legal closed regions.

Segmentation preserves bytes and internal relative branches. It does not
invent branch relaxation or spill code. If a branch or live volatile value
spans the required cut, the selected target needs another declared lowering.

source_files.module_doc:
Bind complete-row scheduling to selected numerical and resource contracts.

The source algorithm is matched, never selected from a hardware lane count.
RTL bounds storage, chunks and integer representation. Software declares each
primitive's complete operands and effects. Execution still needs independent
qualification, including the exponential and ordered rounded arithmetic.

Complete-domain row normalization in the existing counted schedule IR.

The source selects the rounded exponential, lane accumulation order, final
binary tree and normalization operation. Hardware selects chunk limits and
private, addressable storage. A chunk never owns a denominator. Unknown costs
select the largest legal chunk; this is a command-count policy, not a cycle
estimate. Encoders and actual-operand projectors require independent qualification.

symbols.name: RowSoftmaxUnavailable
symbols.doc: Preserve the existing source route; this family cannot realize it.

symbols.name: RowSoftmaxNumerics
symbols.doc:
An explicit source algorithm, not an accuracy or hardware certificate.

Lane j starts with exponential j, then adds j+lanes, j+2*lanes, ... .
First assignment is not an addition to zero. The tree fixes every rounded
addition. Finite unmasked scores, RNE, nontrapping operations and unobserved
floating status are prerequisites of this family. The exponential accepts
nonpositive values including negative infinity and returns exact zero for it.

symbols.name: CausalRowMask
symbols.doc: Column c is active iff c <= row % period + offset; every row is nonempty.

symbols.name: RowSoftmaxStep
symbols.doc:
Public synchronous primitive semantics, with actual physical byte operands.

maximum scans source scores in increasing column order from the retained
-infinity seed. exponential uses the completed row maximum and writes each
shifted exponential once. sum resumes the globally indexed source lanes;
it never resets at a chunk boundary. finish uses the complete source tree,
storing either reciprocal or denominator as selected. normalize reads that
single complete-row result. Masked scores are -infinity in both score passes.
No other effects, reassociation, hidden scratch or state are permitted.

Payload effects are part of this contract: maximum reads count inputs and
reads/writes its scalar once; exponential reads count inputs and one maximum
and writes count scratch elements; sum reads count scratch and reads/writes
all source lanes once; finish reads all lanes and writes one factor;
normalize reads count scratch and one factor and writes count outputs.
Initializers only write their scalar/all lanes. Masked input positions are
still requested. These are logical requests, not bus or register traffic.

symbols.name: allocate_row_softmax_storage
symbols.doc:
Use Merlin's allocator over inclusive completed-phase lifetimes.

Exponential storage holds one full row and is reused only after synchronous
normalization finishes. Maximum/normalizer may share physical bytes; lanes
and normalizer are simultaneously live during finish. Reservations include
packing scratch/DMA staging and apply across aliased bank views.

symbols.name: read_source_rows
symbols.doc:
Match the complete existing pinned source algorithm, including its tree.

This first source family is the explicit f32 CPU algorithm already provided
by cpu_softmax. It supplies no source exponential, lane count or mask from
hardware facts. Other source algorithms retain their original route.
Finite admission applies to this island's actual input, not its producers.

symbols.name: compile_source_rows
symbols.doc:
Bind current typed source to the existing complete-row compiler.

Target instruction selection, realization and independently qualified runtime
bindings remain explicit. Unsupported source raises RowSoftmaxUnavailable
before encoding, leaving the caller's original source route available.

symbols.name: compile_row_softmax
symbols.doc:
Execute admission, tiling, allocation and verified dependency scheduling.

Explicit chunks are Phase-2 alternatives through the same pipeline, selected
source algorithm and checks. Invalid explicit ordering fails before any
encoder/allocation runs. Refusal retains the caller's original source route.
This synchronous schedule-to-C path is not final machine-byte conformance
or ordinary full-model target integration.

source_files.module_doc:
Reconstruct complete row reductions from actual projected counted calls.

This checker admits one bounded grammar, independently of selected chunks:
row loop; initialized full maximum; full exponentials; initialized source lanes;
full ordered sum; completed tree; full normalization. Affine byte operands and
constant chunk counts establish coverage without enumerating tensor elements.
It proves the schedule under the qualified primitive contract, not that an
arbitrary primitive implementation obeys that contract.

symbols.name: verify_row_softmax
symbols.doc: Validate actual phases, operands, domains, state lifetimes and requests.

source_files.module_doc:
Execute checked schedule passes through final independently decoded bytes.

This entry supports finite straight-line byte-addressed programs. Target
encoding and semantic decoding remain selected, independently qualified
capabilities. Unknown instructions, hidden effects and counted loops retain
their separate lowering routes; opaque output is never interpreted here.

symbols.name: ScheduleEncoding
symbols.doc:
Selected target implementation and actual-byte semantic decoder.

decode_calls must reconstruct every instruction's actual operands from
bytes alone, without consulting the optimizer's retained request stream.
This family maps one decoded instruction to one schedule call. Qualification
establishes that all state and numerical semantics are represented.

symbols.name: PostStorageRewrite
symbols.doc:
One original-host deletion transport, not qualification or a manager.

Only the original host selects the live optimizer and separate verifier.
Neither construction nor records grant permissions; author request data
cannot choose these callbacks, source owners or verification premises.

symbols.name: CopyPipelineMotion
symbols.doc:
One original-owner qualified copy-motion slot, separate from deletion.

The base owns placement, stage order, exact membership and final completion.
A reviewed companion supplies the actual algorithm and separate law checker.
Records create neither qualification nor candidate import permissions.

symbols.name: _rewrite_snapshot
symbols.doc: Read original typed data without invoking its record/provider methods.

symbols.name: _program_completions
symbols.doc:
Project exact waits onto the finalizer's qualified global-drain model.

The storage checker remains responsible for token validity and hazards.
A final decoder's drain cannot stand in for a wait for only some pending
operations: that would permit an unsafe cut and storage reuse after launch.

symbols.name: _emission_effects
symbols.doc: Reconstruct complete effects from actual output, independently of requests.

symbols.name: compile_schedule
symbols.doc:
Allocate, check, encode and finalize through the existing pass session.

Missing capabilities or infeasible allocation diagnose for the caller's
existing legal route. Never emit a partially verified candidate. Target
execution qualification is separate from shared transformation correctness.

source_files.module_doc:
Bind schedule passes to selected RTL facts and software/ISA bytes.

RTL references supply structural bounds; software supplies computation,
layouts, effects and ordering for the existing planners. Neither a declaration
nor a review label qualifies execution.

symbols.name: _resolver_sources
symbols.doc: Resolved declarations expire with their shared consumers and checkers.

symbols.name: read_scheduling_contracts
symbols.doc:
Read explicit inputs once and reuse the existing fact-bound ISA resolver.

Only this scheduling extension is interpreted here. Operation admission,
numerical references and execution qualification remain separate owners.
Unknown instructions are barriers, not inferred from their names.

symbols.name: _resolve_declarations
symbols.doc: Shared declaration semantics; selection policy remains in _parse.

symbols.name: scheduling_spec_draft
symbols.doc:
Copy an authored document into an explicitly incomplete construction draft.

No input files, facts, ISA pins or effects are rewritten. An explicit ISA
candidate can fill an absent section; it cannot replace a different one.
