Nulls are questions for the author, not conservative executable defaults.

symbols.name: inspect_scheduling_draft
symbols.doc:
Validate draft declarations through the ordinary resolver, without selecting them.

Returns data only, never SelectedSchedulingContracts or a qualification.
The existing status='reviewed' marker is an author assertion, not an
authenticated review certificate. Draft inspection does not create that
marker or an adapter qualification identity. The ordinary file-based reader
retains its selection checks and byte/source freshness behavior.

source_files.module_doc:
Recognize closed sibling contractions of one immutable typed tensor value.

These source proposals preserve every operation and each independent result.
They establish no physical aliases, target instruction effects or timing.

symbols.name: grow_shared_input_group
symbols.doc:
Yield consecutive prefixes, adding one sibling at a time; never subsets.

Each prefix retains its own exact zero initializers and output identities.
Unselected siblings and external consumers stay in the original module.
``verify_current`` rederives the maximal group before accepting a prefix.

symbols.name: find_shared_input_groups
symbols.doc:
Group adjacent checked zero-seed regions with the identical LHS SSA value.

No operation moves across unknown effects or an intervening consumer. The
existing strict source checker establishes signed products, increasing K,
ordinary tensor layouts and one-use exact zero initializers. Only source
zero/initializer/contraction operations may occur within a group. Grouping
does not erase them or change any use list, including later epilogues.

source_files.module_doc:
Retain one full-reduction input stripe across independent sibling outputs.

The source supplies immutable tensor value identity, exact products and zeros;
the caller selects primitive dimensions and already assigned private storage.
No target instruction, completion rule or physical source/output alias proof
is supplied. Actual target projection must pass the independent checker.

symbols.name: SharedInputEffect
symbols.doc:
Actual logical effect, with distinct RHS/output ownership per sibling.

``member=None`` is reserved for reads of the common immutable input.
A member index selects the source contraction ordinal in the checked group.

symbols.name: _storage
symbols.doc: Check all assigned intervals, including padding and shared backings.

symbols.name: schedule_shared_input
symbols.doc:
Construct and check a bounded raw-core sibling schedule, or decline.

All K tiles of an M panel stay in LHS storage while distinct RHS panels
stream through a bounded output wave. Each output retains increasing K,
its own exact zero seed and its original result identity. Later epilogues
remain separate. No weight/output concatenation or host packing is needed.

``selected_block=(M,K,N)`` exposes a legal choice to an external tuner.
Without it, requested logical bytes, command count and storage break ties.
Counts are not physical traffic/cycles. This finite family declines when
a full-K LHS stripe does not fit; it emits no compact machine loop or fence.

source_files.module_doc:
Independent finite source/lifetime induction over actual sibling effects.

This checks the synchronous logical effect family, not target admission or
overlap. An adapter must decode actual emitted addresses and source bindings;
retaining planned operations instead of projecting emitted ones is no proof.

symbols.name: verify_shared_input
symbols.doc:
Check all source products, separate results and actual private addresses.

Loaded row intervals carry original tensor identities. Every consumed
rectangle is reconstructed from them, including retained array contents.
Accumulator rows carry output ownership and the next required K position.
This proves increasing, complete products without expanding M*K*N scalar
products. Complete output intervals are checked independently at the end.

source_files.module_doc:
Bounded lexical spans for compiler-owned LLVM source proposals.

No assembler, subprocess, target lookup, reference or qualification is exposed.
The lexical productions match the existing late-legalization reader; consuming
these spans establishes no semantic or executable-program proof.

symbols.name: llvm_tokens
symbols.doc:
LLVM punctuation, comments, identifiers and quoted strings with spans.

This is an intentionally small lexer, not a permissive LLVM module parser.
LLVM's assembler verifies the whole module at the public build seam. The
matcher below accepts only explicit instruction productions with typed
operands and a recognized statement boundary.

source_files.module_doc:
Exact device-transfer contract and independent interval provenance checking.

The checker reconstructs byte provenance from actual decoded instructions, not
from a spill plan. It operates on written intervals, never tensor elements or
individual bytes. Opaque arithmetic keeps its original operation order and
decoded nonaddress semantics. Only independently qualified exact private copies
may be inserted or, when selected explicitly, omitted between those operations.
Omission propagates original byte definitions and compares every retained
operation's actual inputs and all external state.

symbols.name: SpillClass
symbols.doc:
Explicit device register class and exact supported spill/reload pair.

This is an independently selected target capability, not host CPU register
allocation. Width and alignment are bytes; both directions must preserve
every bit and complete synchronously. The emitter belongs to the target.

symbols.name: verify_storage_dataflow
symbols.doc:
Compare actual original dataflow and actual final storage byte provenance.

Target qualification establishes the decoder's operation/copy semantics.
This checker establishes their preservation, not machine-code conformance
or target execution qualification. It accepts no selected spill locations.

symbols.name: verify_device_spills
symbols.doc: Verify exact device spill insertion without permitting operation removal.

source_files.module_doc:
Bind device spill capabilities to selected resource and software contracts.

Reuse the existing spill planner and actual-byte provenance checker. Only
addressable device byte registers and independently qualified synchronous,
bit-preserving transfers enter that planner. No host register allocation or
latency estimate is inferred from a resource declaration.

symbols.name: resolve_spill_contract
symbols.doc: Resolve explicit device roles and exact ISA transfers over selected banks.

source_files.module_doc:
Finite staged contraction proposals under independently checked effects.

Unlike dense-v1, a descriptor issue is not synchronous completion. The target
must independently bind these logical effects to its current emitted program;
this library supplies no target lookup, adapter admission or timing authority.

symbols.name: eliminate_redundant_rhs_loads
symbols.doc:
Keep an immutable panel only while its exact private cells remain live.

This does not allocate another panel, prefetch, remove a fence or pretend a
pending descriptor completed. LHS loads invalidate aliased operand cells.

symbols.name: rewrite_staged_dense
symbols.doc:
Apply actual ordered candidate code; independently check every result.

The original target owner must later bind and check the final emitted code.
A successful logical proposal is not that final executable evidence.

symbols.name: order_output_tiles_n_before_m
symbols.doc:
Move complete output tiles to column-major traversal without new storage.

Each movable tile includes its zero, full reduction, readout and following
completion fence. No operation inside a tile is reordered, and no fence is
removed. A later RHS-residency rewrite can use the resulting panel locality.
If earlier rewrites removed a needed load, the independent checker must
reject the resulting proposal; pass order is therefore observable.

source_files.module_doc: Repository compatibility import; frozen SDK API is staged_dense.

Independent finite staged data/descriptor/accumulator state induction.

The target supplies checked effect projection from current actual emitted
operands. No plan claim, pass implementation or configuration label proves
these effects. This checker provides no asynchronous overlap or timing model.

Place RHS panels in an already assigned private full-reduction stripe.

This is a finite proposal, not an allocation or ownership proof. The original
target must independently assign the expanded operand rows for this complete
source epoch, render the changed addresses, and check actual emitted effects.
No hardware capacity, target lookup, synchronization or timing is supplied here.

symbols.name: place_rhs_stripe
symbols.doc:
Preserve all effects while assigning each RHS K panel distinct rows.

Compose through ``rewrite_staged_dense`` so the unchanged independent
source/product/state checker verifies the original and proposed programs.
Complete output-tile ordering and live-load elimination are separate passes;
their order determines whether the new placement saves any transfers.

source_files.module_doc:
Bind private allocation to RTL windows and complete software memory effects.

This is admission and actual-operand projection for the existing allocator, not
another allocation algorithm. Runtime ownership and target execution still need
independent qualification. Source addresses may be virtual before relocation.

symbols.name: binding_value
symbols.doc: Evaluate an already resolved byte/count binding over actual operands.

symbols.name: resolve_operand_binding
symbols.doc: Select an encoded typed operand; never infer a pointer unit.

symbols.name: resolve_element_count
symbols.doc: A bounded product of explicit logical dimensions, not a scalar language.

symbols.name: PrefetchAdmission
symbols.doc: Original qualified overlap pairs; capacity alone grants no overlap.

symbols.name: TemporaryStorageContract
calls: _json((call.instr, declaration['semantics'], preserved, effect.semantic_key, asdict(state) if state is not None else None)).encode
hashlib.sha256(_json((call.instr, declaration['semantics'], preserved, effect.semantic_key, asdict(state) if state is not None else None)).encode()).hexdigest

symbols.name: _reservations
symbols.doc: Union overlapping typed reservations in canonical backing coordinates.

source_files.module_doc:
Relocate private temporaries using actual effects and the existing allocator.

This finite straight-line family uses byte-addressed banks and real completion
instructions. Target adapters decode actual operands and rewrite addresses;
Merlin derives lifetimes, allocates and independently checks realized effects.
It never supplies CPU register allocation or infers effects from opcode names.

symbols.name: StorageOptimizationUnavailable
symbols.doc: Retain the original route: this storage family lacks required information.

symbols.name: TemporaryObject
symbols.doc:
One invocation-private backing allocation, including all of its views.

Source addresses are virtual before allocation. Multiple typed bank views
with the same physical backing use a common byte coordinate system. An
object cannot escape, be a published output or carry invocation state.

symbols.name: StorageEffects
symbols.doc:
Decoded effects, including nonaddress semantics and actual completion.

semantic_key identifies all nonrelocated behavior, including arithmetic,
conversions, external pointer operands and configuration changes. The
adapter's independent qualification must establish this interpretation.
A wait establishes completion and visibility of its named actual tokens.

symbols.name: _completion
symbols.doc: Actual source/realized hazards; an issue-only instruction is not a wait.

symbols.name: _prefetch_crosses
symbols.doc: Qualified overlap is necessary in addition to physical independence.

symbols.name: verify_copy_prefetch
symbols.doc: Verify actual call membership and every inverted dependence, not a plan.

symbols.name: prefetch_private_copies
symbols.doc: Move existing qualified async input copies; preserve launches and waits.

symbols.name: verify_temporary_storage
symbols.doc: Infer addresses from actual output; never accept the selected plan as proof.

symbols.name: allocate_temporary_storage
symbols.doc:
Allocate, consume addresses in actual calls, then independently verify.

Infeasible storage returns None for the caller's existing legal route.
Unsupported effects/ownership and unavailable checking diagnose precisely.
By default, forward exact private copies before allocation; retain the
original composition when its longer source lifetime cannot be allocated.
This entry neither expands loops nor schedules away required completion.

source_files.module_doc: Coalesce contiguous matrix columns into explicitly strided local tile rows.

Prove a convolution window's rows form one in-bounds affine DMA rectangle.

This target-neutral index calculation supplies only a predicate, first logical
element and row stride. The caller retains its scalar gather for every rejected
run and owns the physical transfer, element width and target qualification.

Find closed source initialization groups without selecting a target schedule.

An exact zero splat used only as a signed contraction's seed can remain virtual
when the target independently realizes zero accumulation and complete readout.
These source proposals grant no hardware, ownership or numerical authority.
The selected shared-library releases and their import rosters stay unchanged.

symbols.name: ZeroInitializerGroup
symbols.doc: Current source operations that one checked device task may own together.

symbols.name: find_zero_initializer_groups
symbols.doc:
Propose contiguous one-use zero splat and exact signed rank-two MAC groups.

The source remains unchanged, including every scalar operation and result.
A consumer must keep full source-op/task accounting while omitting virtual
storage, and independently check its actual initializer/readout realization.
Shared constants may stay in another task; shared or returned splats cannot
disappear. Unknown scalar, layout, aliasing or arithmetic semantics retain
the original route. No model identity or provenance label selects a group.

source_files.module_doc:
Checked pointwise destination forwarding for ordinary serial host lowering.

The source's scalar arithmetic is retained. Decisions use static tensor
geometry, source effects, the selected index width and bounded IR growth.
Physical ownership and allocation remain the upstream bufferizer's job.

symbols.name: implementation_paths
symbols.doc: Existing pass-owner closure, also retained through ordinary final linking.

source_files.module_doc:
Ordinary captured-policy host legalization through shared pass contracts.

The source language's canonical pure arithmetic is the numerical contract here.
This route changes no selected quantization model, floating environment policy,
device code, reduction order, or approximation. Unknown scalar effects decline.

symbols.name: optimize_host_quantization
symbols.doc:
Return private, independently checked IR and observations from that IR.

The supplied identity binds the selected original policy; it grants no new
semantics. Eligibility is restricted to canonical tensor scalar bodies with
no unknown effects, attributes or floating-environment operations.

symbols.name: prepare_automatic_host
symbols.doc: Consume the ordinary frozen-policy selection; preserve the input file.

source_files.module_doc:
Compact exact rounding for bounded integer observations in serial host IR.

The selected native LLVM toolchain implements its standard roundeven intrinsic.
This source rewrite makes no ISA, rounding-mode, latency or device-support claim.
Other opaque operations remain barriers. Destination selection runs beforehand.

Select checked row scheduling only for the ordinary serial CPU pipeline.

Source arithmetic is the numerical algorithm; no framework exponential, sum
tree, approximation or target capability is inferred. Unknown source syntax or
unsupported lowering modes retain the original program with a diagnostic.

Store each weight once in a whole-model image: device-layout weights live in the weights blob.

A routed group's device call reads its stored weight in the layout the device program holds it
(:func:`merlin.xdsl_dialects.lowering.group_prepack.prepack`). By default the rewrite hands that copy
over as an ``arith.constant`` (:mod:`merlin.llvmlower.group_host_call`), which lands in the model
object's ``.rodata`` -- while the weights blob keeps the capture's original bytes, whose only reader
was the relayout the rewrite just removed. Every routed weight is then in the image twice (TinyLlama:
1.03 GB of ``.rodata`` beside a 1.30 GB blob).

With :class:`WeightArgs` the rewrite binds each laid-out weight to a TRAILING ``@forward`` argument
instead -- the channel ``qinner`` and ``quant_hoist`` already use, so the C runtime appends the bytes to
the blob and adds the argument rows -- and records which original arguments lost their last reader.
:func:`compact` then drops those arguments' bytes from the blob (their descriptors point at the blob's
base and are never read). Numerics are untouched: the device reads the same bytes from another address.

Written beside the prepared module (``prepared_dir``), read by :func:`merlin.llvmlower.c_runtime.generate`:

- ``blob_weights.json`` -- ``{"args": [{key, shape, dtype}...], "dead_args": [original arg index...]}``
- ``blob_weights.npz``  -- the laid-out bytes, keyed by ``key``

symbols.name: requested
symbols.doc: Within this scope a device group rewrite binds laid-out weights as blob arguments.

symbols.name: _used
symbols.doc:
Indices of ``block``'s arguments some LIVE op reads (transitively from a root, nested regions too).

An argument read only by a dead value chain -- a weight's dequantize-and-requantize that fed the
group the rewrite replaced, left for canonicalization to erase -- is not used.

symbols.name: WeightArgs
symbols.doc:
Binds laid-out device weights to trailing ``@forward`` arguments of ``module`` (one per distinct
tensor); :meth:`finish` seals the function type and the plan.

symbols.name: Plan
symbols.doc: A prepared module's blob weights: the trailing argument rows and the dropped original arguments.

symbols.name: read
symbols.doc: The plan beside a prepared module, or an empty one. Plan without values is an error.

symbols.name: compact
symbols.doc:
``(header, payload)`` without the tensors only ``dead_args`` read.

A tensor stays when any live argument names it (a tied weight read by host code keeps its bytes).
Kept tensors are re-placed ``ALIGNMENT``-aligned in their original order; a dropped tensor's offsets
become ``(0, 0)``, so its never-read descriptor points at the blob's base. A tensor larger than the
final blob (what remains plus the ``appended`` bytes generation adds after it) is kept, so even a dead
read that survived into the object stays inside the image.

source_files.module_doc:
Generate the data-driven inputs the Merlin C runtime needs to drive a compiled model.

The C runtime (`merlin/runtime/c/merlin_model.c`) is generic: it builds MLIR memref
descriptors from an **argument table** and invokes the model's C interface. This module
emits, from the model's MLIR signature + safetensors manifest:

- ``model_gen.h``   — the arg table (kind, weight-blob offset, rank, dims, elem size) +
                      the output shape; consumed by the generic runtime.
- ``model_call.c``  — ``merlin_invoke(void **descs)`` unrolling the N-pointer
                      ``_mlir_ciface_forward`` call (C has no >1024-arg limit, but the
                      arity is model-specific, so it is generated once here).
- ``weights.bin``   — the raw safetensors payload (weights blob; mmap/embed as-is).
- ``model_io.h``    — embedded runtime inputs, output buffers, and optional state-carry map.

Nothing here is target-specific: the same artifacts feed the host and the spike builds.

symbols.name: _align_weight_rows
symbols.doc:
Repair native element alignment without changing any weight alias relation.

Captured byte offsets need not satisfy the native typed-load ABI. Relocate
each affected overlapping component together; never split views or infer
device DMA alignment. Already aligned components retain their exact bytes
and offsets. Lazy span copies keep build memory bounded by the I/O chunk.

symbols.name: manifest_requires_weight_blob
symbols.doc:
Whether any forward argument reads bytes from ``weights.safetensors``.

Stub parameters receive a generated zero region and runtime inputs are embedded separately, so
neither requires a source blob. Externalized buffers do: they name a ``weight`` entry just like
an ordinary parameter.

symbols.name: _out_specs
symbols.doc: Read the result ABI through the shared content-qualified signature cache.

symbols.name: _bf16_bits
symbols.doc:
Round float32 to bfloat16 (round-to-nearest-even) and return the raw uint16 bit patterns.

numpy has no native bf16, so do it by hand: bf16 is the top 16 bits of the f32 encoding; RNE
adds the round bias 0x7FFF + (lsb of the kept mantissa) before truncating. NaNs are preserved
(their exponent is all-ones and mantissa nonzero, which survives the shift).

symbols.name: _storage_nbytes
symbols.doc: Size of the emitted C storage, independent of the capture container dtype.

symbols.name: _storage_bytes
symbols.doc: Expected embedded storage words, without interpreting them as answers.

symbols.name: generate
symbols.doc:
Emit the runtime-driving artifacts for a captured model into ``out_dir``.

Non-weight args are embedded as C arrays: real inputs from ``inputs_npz`` (by order),
and non-persistent buffers / lifted constants (rotary inv_freq, etc.) from
``extra_npz`` (matched by manifest name; ``buf::`` keys for buffers, bare keys for
lifted constants). Weights stay in the blob, referenced by offset.

``prepared_dir`` is the authority for build-time ABI additions emitted while rewriting the
captured module. It is deliberately separate from ``out_dir``, which only receives generated C
artifacts. Callers that do no preparation may leave it unset.

``max_session_steps`` caps how many steps of a session corpus are embedded (streams and the
correctness/quality references together, so step k still meets reference k). ``None`` embeds the
whole corpus, which is what every existing caller gets.

Hash-only generation derives the complete blob without writing it. Explicit
``weights_source`` may share immutable bytes only after exact verification.
All writes replace atomically, so regenerating an output cannot overwrite
an existing shared inode. Mutable invocation state is never shared here.

source_files.module_doc:
The ENVIRONMENT the compiler ran under — recorded, because it changes what gets emitted.

A configuration that does not determine the binary is not a configuration. Two beam nodes carrying
BYTE-IDENTICAL ``knobs.yaml`` (same ``compiler_features``, same ``dtype_strategy``) on the same
capture bundle emitted two different binaries -- digests ``210dbfe9a01c44aa`` and
``2efd837676ff75cd`` -- and ran 2,555,462 ns against 4,151,146 ns, a 1.61x difference that no
recorded field could explain. Nothing in either run's artifacts named the environment.

The lowering path reads a couple of dozen ``MERLIN_*`` variables, and several of them steer codegen
directly rather than merely selecting a host or a path: the per-op block cap, the vectorize-rank
tagging, the OPU packing block and alignment, the worker stack size. An unset-vs-set difference in
any of them changes the emitted code while leaving every recorded field identical.

So the snapshot is taken by PREFIX rather than from a list of names. A curated list is exactly the
thing that goes stale -- the next variable someone adds is the one that is not on it, and its
absence is silent -- and the cost of capturing a few irrelevant variables is nothing next to the
cost of a binary nobody can reproduce.

symbols.name: snapshot
symbols.doc:
Every ``MERLIN_*`` variable that is SET, with sensitive values redacted.

Unset variables are omitted rather than recorded as empty: "not set" and "set to empty string"
are different inputs to the compiler, and conflating them would make the record lie about which
one produced the binary.

symbols.name: digest
symbols.doc: A short stable digest of the snapshot, for comparing two runs at a glance.

symbols.name: cache_digest
symbols.doc:
Bind raw project controls without publishing their values.

The human-readable snapshot intentionally loses redacted and long values.
Its digest cannot authorize cache reuse. JSON framing also distinguishes
embedded newlines and unset versus empty controls. This identity does not
bind referenced files, non-project environment, tools or dependencies.

symbols.name: differences
symbols.doc:
``{name: (a_value, b_value)}`` for every variable the two snapshots disagree on.

``None`` on a side means the variable was NOT SET there, which is the difference that is easiest
to miss and the one most likely to explain two binaries from one recorded configuration.

source_files.module_doc:
Observe owned compiler/link invocations and their actual file inputs/outputs.

This is compilation evidence, not a hermetic toolchain lock or a cache identity.
Headers, library resolution, imported providers and non-project environment need
their own closure. An explicit linker trace may bind named symbol suppliers;
none are inferred by default. Callers name inputs, never a target ABI here.

symbols.name: CompilationRecipe
symbols.doc: One build's observed commands, completed only after the caller's audits.

symbols.name: verify_recipe_schema_and_timing
symbols.doc:
Check supported observation/timing structure without claiming current products.

Offline consumers may retain a successful process observation after its
transient objects and ELF were discarded. This validates the same schema
and timing documents as current-byte verification; it reopens no product
and supplies no compilation, execution or numerical qualification.

symbols.name: verify_completed_recipe
symbols.doc:
Recheck a completed v1/v2 observation against current explicit file bytes.

Imported headers, ambient tool dependencies and numerical behavior are not
inferred. A supplier claim requires the opt-in trace plus an independent
``expected_link_suppliers`` selection; argv archive presence alone is not proof.

``once`` defers only the terminal command output's content read to the
existing final executable check after exact metadata equality. No tool or
callback runs between these checks. ``repeated`` retains both reads as an
explicit comparison mode. Every call freshly hashes the final executable;
neither mode supplies a cache or protects against concurrent file writers.

source_files.module_doc:
Select bounded host window packing before ordinary dense discovery.

The budget counts distinct activation-panel payloads, not host RAM or device
memory. The deterministic policy meets that storage bound with the largest
legal panel found within the search budget. Timing and unknown padding costs
remain unknown; qualified device gathers are not inferred from dense support.

symbols.name: prepare_integer_convolution_panels
symbols.doc:
Apply the existing checked serial panel transform using source semantics.

This explicit route selects no device and grants no physical capability.
The consumer separately selects each resulting ordinary integer product.
Metadata, pure weight views and tensor.splat zero seeds are normalized at
this boundary; original unsupported source remains byte-identical.

symbols.name: _padding_cost
symbols.doc: Count a declared zero-fill/insert; unknown producers remain opaque.

symbols.name: normalize_convolution_source
symbols.doc: Return a checked private source or its unchanged legal full route.

source_files.module_doc:
Explicit source-compatible float32 CPU softmax; never enabled by default.

PyTorch2.10 AVX2 uses eight-lane ordered sums, SLEEF exp_u10 and reciprocal
multiplication. This scalar IR preserves that selected numerical policy without
requiring the destination to implement the source vector ISA.
The exponential schedule adapts SLEEF xexpf, revision5a1d179; its Boost
Software License and copyright notice are preserved in NOTICE.

symbols.name: cpu_softmax_sum_order
symbols.doc: The pinned source lane count and ordered binary denominator tree.

symbols.name: cpu_softmax_row_numerics
symbols.doc:
Expose the existing source algorithm to shared counted-row scheduling.

This is source numerical data, not target support or qualification. The
selected exp implementation must realize build_cpu_softmax_exp_nonpositive.

symbols.name: build_cpu_softmax_exp_nonpositive
symbols.doc:
Scalar SLEEF exp_u10 for nonpositive f32, including negative infinity.

NaN/positive arguments are outside the caller-proven domain. Clamp before
integer conversion so underflow inputs cannot introduce conversion poison.
Float status flags are outside this unconstrained floating-point policy.

symbols.name: build_cpu_softmax_lastdim
symbols.doc: Return detached ops and source-compatible softmax along the last axis.

source_files.module_doc:
Reconstruct destination writes and complete unchanged source/effect wiring.

This reader does not call the rewrite's slab generator or consume its report.
In-bounds disjoint rectangles with the full volume prove complete coverage
without enumerating elements. Physical aliasing remains upstream's obligation.

symbols.name: _realization
symbols.doc: Read one actual empty/exterior/interior write sequence from operation IR.

symbols.name: verify_destination_rewrite
symbols.doc: Check every original operation, interface, use and actual replacement.

symbols.name: _permuted_realization
symbols.doc: Reconstruct a direct output permutation without using emitter decisions.

symbols.name: verify_permutation_rewrite
symbols.doc: Check the complete actual program, including all unchanged opaque effects.

source_files.module_doc:
Explicit projection of unused immutable weights from a generated entry ABI.

The prepared tensor SSA, complete argument table and generated caller contract
are separate obligations. Only whole original stored or generated-zero parameters
with no uses after conservative pure DCE are removed. Model inputs, state,
results and prepared trailing arguments retain their order and semantics.
Unknown effects and symbolic escapes remain live or refuse before mutation.
This is not an LLVM liveness heuristic, a default policy or a cycle model.

symbols.name: GeneratedDispatchABI
symbols.doc:
Caller declarations, not facts inferred from an entry's spelling.

Every out-of-module caller must be regenerated from the projected table.
Unknown external callers or address observations cannot use this contract.
Arithmetic DCE needs the same nontrapping/unobserved effects as upstream
ordinary pure tensor optimization; no additional numerical tolerance is used.
Packed weight spans must be read-only and their addresses unobserved. This
avoids changing observable alias or pointer identity when live spans move.

symbols.name: OptionalFileIdentity
symbols.doc: Actual optional source state, including checked absence at its owner path.

symbols.name: derive_entry_argument_table
symbols.doc:
Derive the table shared by normal preparation and C runtime generation.

The original capture, quant-inner lift and build-time quant-hoist all take
part in the identity. Only stored or generated-zero ``param`` entries are candidates;
buffers, inputs and all trailing preparation entries are retained.
Files are read, never copied or rewritten. No caller may fabricate a shorter
table from a final LLVM signature.

symbols.name: plan_entry_weight_projection
symbols.doc: Read-only typed plan; all removability is rederived from prepared SSA.

symbols.name: apply_entry_weight_projection
symbols.doc: Recheck all source/table/caller proofs, then return a projected clone.

symbols.name: prepare_entry_weight_projection
symbols.doc: Normal post-preparation seam; None returns the original path with no I/O.

symbols.name: compact_runtime_rows
symbols.doc:
Generate a fresh retained descriptor table and weight-span pack.

Input/output array ownership is unchanged. Exact duplicate weight spans may
share storage; partially overlapping spans are copied separately. Every live
descriptor keeps all its original element bytes, including rank-zero/tails.
The original captured bundle and manifest remain immutable.

source_files.module_doc:
Observe routed calls through structurally checked borrowed writer wrappers.

This establishes a profiling boundary and pointer-call prototype only. It grants
no writer effect, numerical, ownership, timing or device execution authority.
Unknown transformations retain the existing profiling diagnostic.

symbols.name: _borrowed
symbols.doc: Recognize the existing fresh-writer wrapper shape, without claiming effects.

symbols.name: derive_bindings
symbols.doc:
Check all original function bodies, allowing only routed callee retargeting.

No attribute or supplied report alone selects a source-to-writer mapping.
Original control flow, types, operands and operations must remain identical.
New private wrapper implementations are read separately for their real ABI.

symbols.name: read_bindings
symbols.doc: Reopen original source, current prepared IR and immutable routing identity.

symbols.name: prepare_profile
symbols.doc:
Generate the existing profiler under the actual source/object boundary.

The runtime driver supplies the observed undefined symbols and retains its
own process, compilation and link authority. Returned flags select no target.

source_files.module_doc:
Emit the im2col column matrix ALREADY PANEL-PACKED, so the B operand walks contiguously.

WHAT IS WRONG WITH THE CODE WE EMIT TODAY
-----------------------------------------
model2MLIR rewrites every convolution into ``im2col gather + matmul`` (``prov.conv_path =
"im2col_matmul"``), and it lays the column matrix out as ``[K][M]``: K is the contraction extent,
M = N*Oh*Ow is the parallel extent the schedule vectorizes. The per-op schedule then tiles
``[MR, NR, 0]`` and tiles K by 1, so **K is the innermost loop and the B-operand load walks with row
pitch M**.

MEASURED off the LINKED ELF (``llvm-objdump -d`` of ``merlin_k1``, deepjscc int8, the shipping
feature set), five independent K-loops, each of the form::

    vsetvli zero, zero, e16, m1
    vle8.v  v16, (a4)                  # 16 bytes of B
    lb a3, ...; lb a5, ...; ...        # the MR scalar A loads
    vwmacc.vx v8,  a3, v17
    ...
    addi    a4, a4, 0x100              # <-- B pointer += M bytes
    addi    a0, a0, 0x1
    bne     a4, a2, <top>

with the increments ``0x1000, 0x400, 0x100, 0x100, 0x100`` -- exactly M bytes for M =
4096, 1024, 256, 256, 256. Every K step therefore pulls a fresh 64-byte cache line and consumes
NR = 16 bytes of it: **4.0x cache-line amplification** on the operand the loop streams. This is the
cost XNNPACK's packed-panel GEMM does not pay.

WHAT THIS DOES
--------------
Nothing about the arithmetic changes and no extra pass over memory is added -- the SAME gather writes
the SAME number of elements, in a different order::

    col[k][m]                 ->    col_p[mo][k][mi]        m = mo*NR + mi

so the innermost (K) loop advances the B pointer by NR ELEMENTS, contiguously, and the NR vector
lanes are the NR consecutive ``mi`` that were already the vectorized axis. The gather's own write is
still a linear walk of its output.

Concretely, for a 2-D conv with output ``(N, Oh, Ow)`` and ``Ow = OWO * NR`` the 6-D gather

    col6[c, kh, kw, n, oh, ow]  <- in[n, c, oh*sh + kh*dh, ow*sw + kw*dw]
    collapse-all -> expand [K, M]

is re-emitted as a 7-D gather whose iteration space splits ``ow`` into ``(owo, owi)`` and reorders so
the panel index leads::

    col7[n, oh, owo, c, kh, kw, owi] <- in[n, c, oh*sh + kh*dh, (owo*NR + owi)*sw + kw*dw]
    collapse [[0,1,2],[3,4,5],[6]] -> [MO, K, NR]        MO = N*Oh*OWO,  K = C*kh*kw

and the contraction becomes a 4-dim ``linalg.generic`` (f, mo, mi, k) with

    A   (f, mo, mi, k) -> (f, k)
    Bp  (f, mo, mi, k) -> (mo, k, mi)
    C   (f, mo, mi, k) -> (f, mo, mi)

whose result collapses ``[[0],[1,2]]`` back to ``[F, M]``. Both reshapes are pure row-major
collapses -- views, not copies -- and the accumulator is the SAME ``linalg.fill`` result seen through
an ``expand_shape``, so the zero-initialization is not re-derived (a contraction reading an unfilled
accumulator is a defect this repo has already shipped once).

The matching schedule arm tiles ``[MR, 1, 0, 0]`` then ``[0, 0, 0, 1]`` and vectorizes
``[MR, 1, NR, 1]``: the same MR x NR register block over the same K-by-1 reduction as the matmul arm,
just with the panel index as its own loop. See ``perop_blocks.schedule_text``.

When ``Ow`` is not divisible by ``NR``, complete panels keep that same path.  A second direct gather
and ordinary matmul cover the row remainder at its true width, and both loops insert directly into
the original ``[F, M]`` accumulator.  There is no padded activation, padded whole-result copy, or
out-of-bounds masked load.  The only new index cost is quotient/remainder once per complete panel;
it is outside the gather element loop and contraction K loop.  This is deliberately a narrow tail
rather than padded compute: ResNet-50's 23 formerly refused sites have tails 8 or 12 at NR=16, so
padding them would execute 2x or 1.33x as many tail MACs for values that are immediately discarded.

WHERE NR COMES FROM
-------------------
NR is NOT chosen here and is never a literal. The caller passes the per-op block table
``perop_blocks.block_table`` already derived for this model -- N tile widened per contraction for the
board's VLEN and that contraction's own narrowest element width (``nr_cap_for_dtypes``:
``vlen // narrowest_elem_bits``) and clipped by the lowering predicate. This pass reads the NR that
table assigned to THIS contraction's geometry and packs to it. A geometry the table did not price has
no NR, so it is refused, not guessed.

WHAT IT REFUSES TO DO (fail closed, and every refusal is counted)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
* a contraction whose B operand is not a single-use ``expand_shape <- collapse_shape <- 6-D
  all-parallel copy generic`` chain (``refused_not_im2col``);
* any operand of that chain with more than one use -- rewriting it would leave the old gather alive
  and pay for both (``refused_shared_value``);
* a gather whose input map is not ``(n, c, sh*oh + dh*kh, sw*ow + dw*kw)`` with non-negative integer
  coefficients, read STRUCTURALLY off the affine expressions (``refused_unreadable_gather_map``);
* a geometry with no entry in the block table (``refused_unpriced``);
* a chosen panel width below two, which cannot improve contiguity
  (``refused_panel_width_too_narrow``);
* an accumulator that is not a ``linalg.fill`` result (``refused_accumulator_not_filled``);
* the grouped (rank-7) im2col form (``refused_not_im2col`` -- its contraction is 4-dim already).

Structure-keyed throughout: no op name beyond the linalg/tensor ops it rewrites, no model name, no
target name, no shape constant, no ``prov.*`` read as a classifier. Default OFF -- with the feature
absent nothing here runs, the block table, the tags and the schedule are byte-identical, and so is
the emitted ``.ll``.

NOT MEASURED ON HARDWARE. The layout change is verified on the emitted code (the B-load pointer
advance in the linked ELF's K loops) and the numerics are verified by output digest; no wall-clock
claim is made here.

symbols.name: PackReport
symbols.doc: What the pass did, and what it refused. Every refusal is named and counted.

symbols.name: _affine_term
symbols.doc: ``(coefficient, dim)`` for ``d`` or ``d * c`` / ``c * d`` with a positive integer ``c``.

symbols.name: _window_term
symbols.doc:
``(stride, dilation)`` for ``s*d<stride_dim> + t*d<kernel_dim>``, else None.

This is the whole geometry read: a conv window is exactly this expression, and reading the two
coefficients off it is what keeps the pass from assuming a stride or a dilation.

symbols.name: _is_copy_body
symbols.doc: The gather's body is a pure element copy: one ``linalg.yield`` of the input block argument.

symbols.name: _match_im2col
symbols.doc: The ``gather -> collapse -> expand -> contraction`` chain, or None with a counted refusal.

symbols.name: _matmul_maps
symbols.doc:
The ordinary ``(m, n, k)`` contraction maps -- the same triple m2m emits for an im2col matmul.

The panel-loop body is a PLAIN contraction of exactly this shape, which is the point: it is priced,
tagged and scheduled by the per-op block machinery that already exists, with no packed-specific
schedule arm, tagger key or op class. A 4-dim ``(f, mo, mi, k)`` generic was tried first and does
NOT lower -- vectorizing it yields a ``vector.contract`` with two N-like parallel dims (``mo``
appears in B and C but not in A, so it is neither a batch dim nor an N dim), which no contraction
lowering strategy handles; it reached LLVM translation as a live
``builtin.unrealized_conversion_cast`` and failed the build.

symbols.name: _dyn_slice_props
symbols.doc: ``static_offsets/sizes/strides`` for a slice with ONE dynamic offset at ``dyn_dim``.

symbols.name: _rewrite_one
symbols.doc: Replace the matched chain in place with the panel-packed one.

symbols.name: _spatial_panel_gather
symbols.doc:
Build a direct gather for ``panel_count`` panels of ``width`` columns in every output row.

``first_ow`` is the first output column covered.  Keeping the output-row dimensions explicit is
important: it avoids a floordiv/mod pair for every im2col element.  Tail support pays index
arithmetic once per contraction panel instead (in :func:`_spatial_panel_loop`).

symbols.name: _spatial_panel_loop
symbols.doc:
Contract packed panels into their unpadded positions in the original ``[F, M]`` result.

The quotient/remainder is evaluated once per panel, never in the K loop or the gather element
loop.  Consequently a non-divisible output width retains the full-width kernel for its complete
panels and uses one narrower kernel only for each row's remainder.

symbols.name: _rewrite_one_with_tail
symbols.doc:
Pack full-width panels and a row tail without padding or copying the whole activation/result.

Returns the tail width, which is also the N extent of the second ordinary contraction geometry.

symbols.name: rewrite_module
symbols.doc:
Pack every eligible im2col contraction in ``module`` (mutated in place).

``table`` is the per-op block table already derived for THIS model
(``perop_blocks.block_table``); the NR it assigned to a contraction's geometry is the panel width
used for that contraction. A geometry the table did not price is refused.

symbols.name: _accumulator_is_filled
symbols.doc:
The contraction's ``outs`` must be a ``linalg.fill`` result.

A contraction accumulates into its output, so an ``outs`` that is a bare ``tensor.empty`` reads
undefined memory. Today m2m always emits the fill; requiring it here means the reshaped
accumulator this pass builds cannot silently become the un-zeroed one.

symbols.name: rewrite_prepared_file
symbols.doc:
Pack ``prepared`` and write ``model.bpacked.mlir``; returns ``(path, report)``.

Runs in merlin's own interpreter over xDSL -- the same library that BUILT these ops in
model2MLIR -- and BEFORE ``perop_blocks.tag_prepared_mlir``, which round-trips the module through
the MLIR printer. Nothing is written when nothing was packed: the caller keeps the original path,
so a run where every candidate was refused is byte-identical to the baseline rather than
re-serialized.

symbols.name: ensure_registered
symbols.doc:
Register the default-off :data:`FEATURE` request. Idempotent.

Registered from HERE and called by the preparation step, ``llvmlower.lower`` and
``pipeline.lower_to_llvm_ir``, for the reason ``perop_blocks.ensure_registered`` records: the
lowering runs in a child process that re-imports the feature registry, and a name registered only
in the parent fails to resolve in the child. It also has to be registered before
``wholemodel_proposer._composes`` is asked about it -- that helper swallows the ``KeyError`` for an
unregistered name and answers False, so an unregistered lever is never proposed and never
complains.

symbols.name: BoundedIm2ColSource
symbols.doc: Original typed source witness, frozen before the old island is erased.

symbols.name: match_bounded_im2col
symbols.doc:
Read a sole-use static integer island without granting device gathers.

The ordinary dense reader owns the scalar recurrence and exact zero seed.
This extra admission checks the actual window/reshape maps and motion scope.
Unsupported source retains its full materialization route.

symbols.name: bounded_source_identity
symbols.doc: Identity for the original analysis stamp, before any source mutation.

symbols.name: rewrite_bounded_match
symbols.doc:
Reuse a fixed activation panel in each serial main/tail loop.

The host owns the explicit sum-of-panel payload budget. This transformation
grants neither a device gather nor asynchronous operand retention.

symbols.name: verify_bounded_match
symbols.doc:
Reconstruct the realized affine windows, complete output coverage and reuse.

Original pass analyses supply expected_source and expected_bindings to bind
the witness and external SSA values to their immutable current-source context.
These source-level tensor destinations establish neither allocation nor timing.

source_files.module_doc:
Exact pointwise destination passing into padded or permuted tensors.

Permuted outputs retain scalar order. Static integer dimension splits compose
input coordinates and preserve the original row-major visitation exactly. Each
original producer/transpose pair is visited once; generated writers are not candidates.

The scalar body is cloned unchanged. Static unit-stride slices, an unused output
block argument, a sole tensor-result use, and pure arithmetic are required.
A fresh fill gives the padded destination writable storage; an extract-slice is
then the producer's destination. Bufferization owns alias legality.

The explicit ``initialize_border_only`` option fills the disjoint rectangular
complement instead. The unread interior is completely overwritten by the same
scalar producer. A live original splat remains immutable and separate. This
option changes no arithmetic, input layout, call ABI, or default selection.

symbols.name: exterior_slabs
symbols.doc:
Disjoint rectangular complement of one in-bounds rectangular interior.

Earlier dimensions are restricted to the interior; the current dimension
selects its lower or upper exterior. Every exterior point therefore belongs
to the slab for its first out-of-interior dimension, exactly once.

symbols.name: _safe_source
symbols.doc: Moving scalar arithmetic may cross constants/storage constructors only.

symbols.name: _expanded_coordinates
symbols.doc: Exact static contiguous dimension splits; no padding or duplicated lanes.

symbols.name: rewrite_permuted_outputs
symbols.doc:
Forward sole-use pointwise results into their permuted destinations.

Direct permutations retain input maps and loop order. An optional static
integer expansion splits dimensions with exactly the original row-major
visitation; scalar instructions remain unchanged and execute once per point.
The final logical value/type and every consumer ABI stay unchanged. This
supplies no target physical packing contract or strided-store timing claim.

symbols.name: rewrite_module
symbols.doc:
Rewrite proved static regions, optionally bounded before constructing IR.

These are IR growth budgets, not hardware dimensions or a cycle estimate.
The standalone unbounded API remains available to explicit callers.

source_files.module_doc:
Fuse a ``roundeven -> clamp -> fptosi`` quantize chain into a rounding-mode-independent
pure-arith convert, so the generic carrying it stops being a scalar libm call site.

WHAT IT IS FOR, and why the size of it is not obvious from the op count.

The int8 activation quantize (``passes_quant_int``, several construction sites, all emitting the
same round/clamp/convert body after a separately materialized reciprocal) is::

    %v = arith.mulf   %x, %inverse_scale    : f32
    %r = math.roundeven %v                  : f32
    %a = arith.minimumf %r, %hi             : f32
    %b = arith.maximumf %a, %lo             : f32
    %q = arith.fptosi %b                    : f32 to i8

Five ops in the IR. But ``math.roundeven`` has no vector form on this path: ``convert-math-to-libm``
turns it into a CALL to ``roundevenf``, and the vector variant of that pass scalarizes a
``vector<Nxf32>`` back into N extracts + N calls + N inserts. So the op is a scalar libm call per
ELEMENT, and everything around it is scalar too because nothing will vectorize a loop containing a
call.

Two consequences, and the second is the one that makes this a lever rather than a cleanup:

1. The chain is expensive. `roundevenf` on this toolchain is a nine-instruction body whose payload is
   `fcvt.w.s` (round-to-nearest-even) followed by `fcvt.s.w` back to float, wrapped in a
   `|x| < 2^23` guard -- a guard that is DEAD here, because the very next ops clamp the result into a
   range where it cannot fire.
2. The chain is a VECTORIZATION BARRIER, and that barrier is enforced twice over. LLVM's loop
   vectorizer declines a loop containing the call; and, upstream of it, the ``merlin.vec_r{rank}``
   TAGGER (`runtime/backends/zephyr_model._prepare_model_mlir`) refuses outright any all-parallel
   generic with a ``math.*`` op in its body -- a refusal that is CORRECT, and that this pass is the
   way past. Its comment says so: those ops "are the OTHER lever's job". The activation lever
   (`vectorized_transcendental_activation`) is the other lever for `math.exp`/`erf`/`tanh`; this is
   the one for the quantize chain, and it composes the same way -- rewrite to pure arith BEFORE the
   tagger runs, and the existing per-rank arms claim the op with no new arm written.

The exact rewrite and explicit MLIR vectorization are deliberately separate feature points.  The
rewrite alone removes the libm barrier and lets LLVM's loop vectorizer claim the resulting ordinary
arithmetic.  ``fuse_quantize_round_convert_vec`` additionally enables Merlin's bounded
``vectorize_non_contraction_generics`` schedule.  Keeping that composition explicit matters: on the
TinyLlama MR4/NR32 packed path the broad schedule changed the proven scalar-feed kernel from
``lb + vwmacc.vx`` into ``lbu + vmv.v.x + vsext + vwmacc.vv``.  A helper feature must not silently
rewrite an unrelated hot contraction while reporting itself as an epilogue optimization.

THE EQUIVALENCE, which is the whole correctness argument and is exact, not approximate.

Write `re` for IEEE roundToIntegralTiesToEven (what ``math.roundeven`` computes -- a specified
operation, NOT affected by the dynamic rounding mode), `C` for the clamp the chain applies, and
`tz` for truncate-toward-zero (what ``arith.fptosi`` computes). The baseline computes `tz(C(re(v)))`.

  LEMMA 1 (the clamp commutes with the rounding). If every clamp bound is an INTEGRAL float, then
  `C(re(v)) = re(C(v))`. `re` is monotone non-decreasing and fixes every integer, so for an upper
  bound `hi`: if `v <= hi` then `re(v) <= re(hi) = hi` and both sides are `re(v)`; if `v > hi` then
  `min(v,hi) = hi` gives `re(hi) = hi` on the right, and on the left `re(v) >= hi` so `min(re(v),hi)
  = hi` as well. Symmetrically for a lower bound. Chains of such bounds compose. This is why the
  pass REFUSES a non-integral bound rather than rounding it: the commutation is the only thing that
  lets the clamp move to where it can bound the argument.

  LEMMA 2 (the truncation is a no-op). `re(u)` is integer-valued, and after Lemma 1 it lies in
  `[lo, hi]`, which the pass has already checked is inside the destination integer type. So
  `tz(re(C(v))) = re(C(v))` exactly -- no truncation happens, and `fptosi`'s round-toward-zero never
  differs from the round-half-to-even that produced its input. This is the step that makes the two
  DIFFERENT rounding rules in the chain collapse into one.

  So the whole chain is exactly: clamp into `[lo, hi]`, then round half-to-even. Checked at every
  boundary the composition has:
    * `v` NaN: `arith.minimumf` is IEEE `minimum` and PROPAGATES NaN, so both forms would reach
      `fptosi(NaN)`, which is POISON in LLVM. They are therefore equivalent only for defined inputs,
      not observationally interchangeable after optimization. In particular, an all-zero activation
      used to give `amax = 0`, `s = 0`, and `0/0 = NaN`. Scale construction now floors `s` to the
      framework's positive epsilon; the matcher follows the tensor producer and accepts only that
      proved floor (or a finite nonzero constant), refusing an unguarded dynamic divisor.
    * `v = +/-inf`: `re` fixes them, the clamp pins them to `hi`/`lo`. The rewrite clamps first and
      gets `hi`/`lo` directly. Same.
    * `|v| >= 2^23`: `v` is already integral, so `re(v) = v` and the clamp pins it to `hi`/`lo`. The
      rewrite clamps first, so it never evaluates the round on a value this large at all -- which is
      exactly what makes the inline round below safe.
    * ties: `v = 126.5 -> 126`, `127.5 -> 127` (rounds to 128, clamps back), `-127.5 -> -127`,
      `-2.5 -> -2`, `2.5 -> 2`, `1.5 -> 2`, `-0.5 -> -0.0 -> 0`. The emitted form reproduces each.

HOW THE ROUND IS EMITTED, and why not the cheaper spellings.

After the clamp, `|c| <= max(|lo|,|hi|)`, which the pass has checked is under 2^23. In that range
round-half-to-even is exactly expressible in ordinary arith, with NO dependence on the dynamic
rounding mode::

    t  = fptosi(c)                # truncate toward zero; exact, |c| < 2^23
    ft = sitofp(t)                # exact
    d  = c - ft                   # EXACT (t is a multiple of ulp(c) when |c| < 2^23), |d| < 1
    bump = |d| > 1/2  or  (|d| == 1/2 and t is odd)
    q  = t + (bump ? sign(c) : 0)

`t` and `q` are computed in the DESTINATION integer type, not in a wider one: `q = re(c)` and
`c` is in `[lo, hi]`, so by Lemma 1's monotonicity `q` is in `[lo, hi]` too, a range the pass has
already required to fit that type -- so neither the convert nor the `+/-1` can overflow, and no
truncation back is needed.

REJECTED, deliberately, and both rejections are about the ROUNDING MODE:

  * the add/sub magic constant (`x + 1.5*2^23 - 1.5*2^23`, which `act_poly._ap_roundeven` uses for the
    exp range reduction). It is two ops instead of fourteen, and it is CORRECT only while the dynamic
    rounding mode is round-to-nearest-even, because it works by asking the FP adder to do the
    rounding. The baseline chain it replaces is rounding-mode INDEPENDENT, so using it here would
    introduce a dependence on `frm` that the code being replaced does not have -- on a target whose
    `frm` this repo neither sets nor derives, and in a pass that is supposed to be target-agnostic.
    (It is also wrong on `[2^22, 2^23)` with that constant, though the clamp hides that.)
  * emitting a float->int convert that names round-to-nearest-even directly. There is no such op in
    `arith` (`fptosi` is truncate, by definition) and reaching for `llvm.intr.*` inside a
    `linalg.generic` body would put an op there that the linalg vectorizer cannot vectorize, which
    defeats the entire purpose. Setting `frm` around the region and using the dynamic mode was
    considered and rejected for the same reason as the magic constant, plus a second one: `frm` is
    process-global state that every other float op in the emitted code reads, so setting it would
    change the rounding of code this pass never looked at.

The sequence below is therefore longer than either, and it is the only one of the three whose result
does not depend on a mode nobody in this repo derives.

TARGET-AGNOSTIC: the matcher names no target, no model, no shape, no dtype and no constant. The clamp
bounds, the destination integer width and the float type are all READ OFF THE IR being rewritten; the
only literals are 1/2 and 1, which are properties of round-half-to-even itself. Anything it cannot
establish -- a non-integral bound, a one-sided clamp, a bound outside the destination type, a value
used more than once, `fptoui` instead of `fptosi` -- is REFUSED and COUNTED, never approximated.

symbols.name: _integral_limit
symbols.doc: The magnitude at which ``float_type`` runs out of fractional bits (2 ** mantissa bits).

symbols.name: _const_float
symbols.doc: Read a float constant through uniform splats and their generic input arguments.

symbols.name: _single_use
symbols.doc:
``value`` feeds exactly one op. Rewriting a chain whose intermediate is read elsewhere would
leave the original `math.roundeven` alive AND add the inline round, which is strictly worse than
doing nothing -- so a shared intermediate is refused rather than duplicated.

symbols.name: _constant_zero
symbols.doc: Prove a zero through casts and uniform splats, including generic input arguments.

symbols.name: _guarded_scale_value
symbols.doc:
Return the scalar yielded by a scale tensor feeding this generic block argument.

Dynamic quantization computes the scale in one ``linalg.generic`` and consumes that tensor in
another.  The divisor visible beside ``roundeven`` is consequently a block argument, not the
guarding ``arith.select`` itself.  Follow exactly that one producer edge; do not guess through
arbitrary tensor computations.

symbols.name: _is_zero_guarded_scale
symbols.doc: Whether ``value`` comes from a proved-positive symmetric scale constructor.

symbols.name: _dynamic_scale_of_quant_input
symbols.doc: Return the scale in ``x / scale`` or TorchAO's ``x * (1 / scale)`` spelling.

symbols.name: _match_chain
symbols.doc:
``(round_op, clamp_ops, lo, hi)`` for a fusable chain ending at ``fptosi_op``, else a reason.

Walks BACKWARDS from the convert through a run of `arith.minimumf` / `arith.maximumf` whose other
operand is an integral float constant, and requires the run to bottom out at `math.roundeven`.
A single-use addition of a constant signed zero is also traversed. It preserves all defined
integer results of this chain; the possible zero-sign change is erased by `fptosi`.
The interval is accumulated in the order the ops apply, so a chain that never bounds one side is
caught rather than assumed.

Returns either a 4-tuple or a string naming the refusal.

symbols.name: fuse_round_clamp_convert
symbols.doc:
Rewrite every fusable ``roundeven -> clamp -> fptosi`` chain in ``module``; returns the count.

Reports refusals BY REASON into ``report_out``. That is not decoration: a pass that rewrote
nothing and a pass that could not reach anything both return 0, and only the counters separate
them -- which is the failure mode this repo keeps re-learning about default-off levers.

symbols.name: ensure_registered
symbols.doc: Register the isolated rewrite and explicit vectorized composition. Idempotent.

source_files.module_doc:
Independent expression reconstruction for bounded quantization legalization.

Only pure, straight-line typed scalar bodies are interpreted. Outer operations,
interfaces, effects and dataflow must remain structurally identical. This is a
conditional arithmetic check at tensor IR, not machine-code or hardware proof.

symbols.name: bounded_round_input
symbols.doc:
Read literal integral clamp bounds for a defined narrow conversion.

No producer, source label or selected plan supplies these bounds. Unknown
scalars stop the walk, and both bounds must already have been established.

symbols.name: residual_round_expression
symbols.doc: Declarative ties-even identity, independent of the instruction emitter.

symbols.name: pure_scalar_body
symbols.doc: Canonical value semantics exclude opaque effects and constrained FP.

symbols.name: verify_quantization_rewrite
symbols.doc: Reconstruct actual output expressions and all unchanged outer effects.

source_files.module_doc:
Explicit backend selection for ordinary checked source preparation.

Merlin matches current typed source, checks schedules and inverts its call
replacement. The original caller supplies target instruction selection, ABI
glue, capability revalidation and independent execution qualification. No
target is discovered and no qualified device implementation is supplied here.

symbols.name: PointwiseSourceBackend
symbols.doc:
Host-selected implementation callbacks; declarations alone qualify nothing.

propose(source, operation, directory) returns ordinary pointwise compilation
kwargs or None for unsupported semantics/layout/resources. emit returns the
independently qualified fresh-writer ABI contract after emitting actual glue.
finalize assembles those fragments. build retains the ordinary checked
HostProviderBuild interface. verify reopens original capability selections.

symbols.name: DenseSourceLimits
symbols.doc: Original source/verification ceilings; policies may only reduce work caps.

symbols.name: DenseSourceBackend
symbols.doc:
Host-owned exact dense implementation; missing runtime proof stays off.

The propose callback receives a freshly matched DenseProblem and current
operation. Merlin supplies source, selected contracts, name and original
runtime ownership to the fixed checked scheduler. No field is a target
qualification issuer; the original independent callback remains mandatory.

symbols.name: SharedSourceBackend
symbols.doc:
One explicitly reviewed implementation for dense and pointwise islands.

Callbacks dispatch on the typed source descriptor, never model identities.
One finalize/build owner sees the complete selected island set, including
supported readouts; this does not imply fusion or device residency.

symbols.name: SharedSourceRouting
symbols.doc: One ordinary preparation/build invocation; missing qualification stays off.

symbols.name: PointwiseSourceRouting
symbols.doc: Compatibility entry retaining the original pointwise-only selection.

symbols.name: resolve_pointwise_provider
symbols.doc: Recognize only this original typed owner, never a callback-selected bypass.

source_files.module_doc:
Discover source contractions for the existing resource-bound dense planner.

Hardware and software contracts constrain the existing planner; a backend only
supplies assigned physical storage and qualified instruction/ABI implementations.
Unsupported computations keep their source route. This interface checks source
and schedule IR, not arbitrary emitted C or machine-code semantics.

symbols.name: SourceDenseLowering
symbols.doc:
Fixed selected resources and implementation bindings for one invocation.

Storage is an allocation output, not permission to occupy an entire memory.
Optional resources restrict the existing search; selected contracts clamp
them to physical limits. Runtime ownership and disjointness are independent
premises, never inferred from distinct tensor SSA values.

symbols.name: offload_context
symbols.doc:
Current whole-source resources, effects and implementation identities.

This scope includes the logical ABI and packing controls as well as dense
scheduling. Callable identities cannot establish implementation equivalence;
the original qualifier and actual provider/product checks remain mandatory.

symbols.name: offload_implementation_paths
symbols.doc: Explicit optional source-binding/cost checker owners; no access grant.

symbols.name: ordinary_dense_route_identity
symbols.doc: Identity of the unchanged ordinary dense route under this source/context.

symbols.name: validate_offload_selection
symbols.doc: Reopen original source/context and cost ownership without granting legality.

symbols.name: discover_dense
symbols.doc: Derive contractions and schedules from current IR; never ask a backend to select regions.

source_files.module_doc:
One model preparation/link transaction for selected shared source families.

Discovery is fixed shared code. Target callbacks receive checked computations
for implementation, never an arbitrary source-selection hook. Families retain
their existing typed IR and pass pipelines; this module only joins their fresh
writer ABI, immutable inputs and ordinary provider/link lifecycle.

symbols.name: SourceRegion
symbols.doc: Internal SSA replacement, not another computation or target IR.

symbols.name: _region_results
symbols.doc:
Check complete output ownership before constructing a replacement call.

Computation/effect admission remains the family's checker. This verifies
only the new plural bridge's SSA membership, placement and observers. The
legacy singleton route keeps its existing last-operation result convention.

symbols.name: _ConvolutionFallback
symbols.doc: Private bounded repair before publishing any provider selection.

symbols.name: bind_source_lowerings
symbols.doc: Select only known source families, through the ordinary existing hooks.

symbols.name: source_borrowed_calls
symbols.doc: Original selected writer effects; no grants from a declaration or target.

source_files.module_doc:
Ordinary model source selection from declared integer scalar semantics.

The software contract supplies eligible arithmetic; target bindings map immutable
typed computations to original instructions and physical buffers. The existing
pointwise compiler independently checks both that original sequence and actual
final decoded bytes. Unknown source/mappings retain the original source route.

symbols.name: PointwiseProgram
symbols.doc: Target instruction selection/mapping under the fixed selected contracts.

symbols.name: discover_pointwise
symbols.doc: Find semantics from software, while instruction mapping remains target-owned.

source_files.module_doc:
Select checked source rows during ordinary model preparation.

The shared compiler discovers and rewrites supported source islands. Explicit
backend bindings implement their primitives and ranked borrowed ABI, including
the declared input, workspace and completion premises. This transport neither
qualifies those bindings nor interprets opaque backend output.

symbols.name: SourceRowLowering
symbols.doc:
Selected capabilities and implementation bindings, never source selection.

``prepare`` receives all checked bindings and an invocation-private directory;
``build`` receives those bindings and the existing HostProviderContext. The
latter returns a HostProviderBuild subject to the ordinary object/link gates.
Finite inputs must be established at each island's actual input, for example
by a qualified runtime guard. Finite model inputs alone are insufficient.

symbols.name: SourceRowBinding
symbols.doc: One checked source computation and its fresh-result borrowed ABI.

symbols.name: discover_rows
symbols.doc: Compile supported canonical regions on the immutable original module.

symbols.name: bind_source_row_lowering
symbols.doc: Compatibility entry for one selected row family.

source_files.module_doc:
Lazy byte spans for the existing generated weight-blob layout.

This is build-time host storage, not a device memory or scheduling contract.
Readers borrow source files/arrays until consumption; callers still own content
freshness and immutable invocation inputs. No content identity is memoized.

symbols.name: WeightPayload
symbols.doc: Ordered file/array/zero spans; slicing and alignment never copy payloads.

source_files.module_doc:
One program's linked whole-model image: built once per submission, relinked per input, run on Spike.

The build is Merlin's ordinary whole-model build (``compile_saved_model``, ``run="none"``, full readback,
group profile) with the submission as the device package, routed exactly as a full-model qualification
routes it (every source-admitted group, :func:`merlin.compile.route_before_build.plan_before_build`).

A new input needs no re-lowering. The build records every compile and link command it ran
(``build/compilation_recipe.json``); the inputs live only in the generated ``cgen/model_io.h``, which
only the driver ``model_main.c`` includes. Relinking for an input therefore regenerates ``cgen`` from a
shadow of the capture whose ``inputs.npz`` is the bound input, checks that everything else it generated
(weights blob, argument table call) is byte-identical to the build's, recompiles ``model_main.o`` with
the recipe's own command and repeats the recipe's link. The shadow carries no session contract, so the
image runs exactly one forward on exactly the bound inputs (a captured session's carried state and
stream are inputs like any other here; the chain supplies them).

symbols.name: FullBuildError
symbols.doc: A program image could not be built, relinked, run or read back.

symbols.name: elf_sections
symbols.doc: ``{section: bytes}`` of every allocated section of a little-endian ELF64 image.

symbols.name: BuildSettings
symbols.doc: How a model's programs are built (the models file's ``full`` blocks; contract §2).

symbols.name: _profile_table_matches
symbols.doc: A profiled image can be reused only with its original adjacent table.

symbols.name: _lowering_sources
symbols.doc:
Direct host pass owners, without importing their implementations.

Bind both source families so adding or editing a pass cannot reuse a prior
default. This is not a transitive dependency or toolchain closure.

symbols.name: _build_inputs
symbols.doc:
Stream current explicit inputs; paths and stat metadata cannot authorize reuse.

Reuse the saved-model compiler's strict tree reader, including policy, state
and unknown files. Read existing selected/scoped facts without extraction.
This is not a transitive provider, native resource or toolchain closure.

symbols.name: _cached_admission
symbols.doc: Evaluate today's selected policy on actual cached bytes, never an old verdict.

symbols.name: _relink_artifacts
symbols.doc: Reopen the existing complete recipe and the driver's shared preparation inputs.

symbols.name: _verify_relink
symbols.doc: Require current origin inputs and actual reusable products before launching a tool.

symbols.name: _routing
symbols.doc: The submission's device routing over every source-admitted group, or ``None`` (host only).

symbols.name: build
symbols.doc:
Build ``stage``'s image under ``directory`` (reused when its record matches) and return its record.

``offload=False`` builds the host twin: the same recipe and host code with every group on the host
and no device object of the submission (the differential's reference image).

Two checks of one submission share the directory: the first builds while holding its lock, the
second waits and reuses the record.

symbols.name: relink
symbols.doc: The build's image with ``inputs`` (``{"in0": ...}``) embedded instead of the capture's; its ELF path.

symbols.name: _relink_native
symbols.doc: The build's image with ``inputs`` (``{"in0": ...}``) embedded instead of the capture's; its ELF path.

symbols.name: discard
symbols.doc: Remove a relinked step's image and generated sources, keeping its bound inputs (``capture/inputs.npz``).

symbols.name: run
symbols.doc:
``(console bytes, wall seconds)`` of ``elf`` on the target's functional simulator, on the machine
the image declares (never the simulator's defaults), within ``timeout_s`` and the backend's own
ceiling for one run.

symbols.name: run_host
symbols.doc:
``(console bytes, wall seconds)`` of a host-only image (a host twin) on the plain functional
simulator with the ISA and memory span the image declares.

A twin issues no accelerator instruction, so it needs no extension -- and it computes every group in
scalar code, which can take longer than the selected engine's ceiling for one submission run
(SmolVLA's prefix: ~1 G MAC/min). Its bound is the check's own time budget.

symbols.name: read
symbols.doc: Every result of the forward (i1 as bool), its text metrics and its group profile.

source_files.module_doc:
Selected final-program checks on a declared section of the actual linked ELF.

This host-only bridge composes with the caller's existing admission policy.
Section selection and independently qualified decoding remain explicit inputs;
it grants no runtime, physical mapping, numerical or timing qualification.

symbols.name: service
symbols.doc:
Add actual-byte checks to an original policy for ordinary build/cache/relink.

``decoder_sources`` must come from the original independently qualified
decoder provider. Source pins record attribution, not qualification. The
reader budget bounds extraction; it never enlarges selected hardware limits.
No section discovery, backend import, segmentation or SDK grant is supplied.

source_files.module_doc:
Whole-model bare-metal execution on spike (multicore RVV CPU).

Builds and runs a captured model end to end on spike:
  model.mlir → LLVM IR (llvmlower) → rv64gcv object (clang)
  + the Merlin C runtime (generic descriptor builder, arg table, bump allocator)
  + weights.bin linked as a binary blob
  → ELF → spike → parse the HTIF bit-exact output → gate vs a reference.

Everything is data-driven and model-agnostic: the arg table and ciface trampoline are
generated from the MLIR signature (`llvmlower.c_runtime`), so any captured model builds
the same way; only the arena size and spike `-m` scale with the model. The output is
emitted as raw f32 bit patterns over HTIF, so the gate is exact up to FP reassociation.

Toolchain via `MERLIN_CHIPYARD` (default /path/to/chipyard); LLVM clang via the
llvmlower `toolchain`.

symbols.name: _mlir_runtime_compiler
symbols.doc:
Use the model compiler's scalar ABI and the environment's C headers.

BF16 compiler helpers use floating registers under Clang's RISC-V ABI.
GCC's unsigned-short fallback uses integer registers and cannot service
these calls, even when both compilers select the same ISA and LP64D ABI.

symbols.name: _selected_libm_archive
symbols.doc:
Resolve the selected driver's archive before naming it as a link input.

A path found by a later diagnostic query is not evidence for an earlier
``-lm`` link. The returned absolute archive is used directly by this build.

symbols.name: declared_harts
symbols.doc: The hart count an image states with :data:`HART_COUNT_SYMBOL`; ``None`` when it states none.

symbols.name: _extension_name
symbols.doc: ``zvl128b1p0`` -> ``zvl128b``, ``m2p0`` -> ``m``: an ELF arch token without its version.

symbols.name: arch_extensions
declared_isa
symbols.doc:
The ``--isa`` a functional simulator needs to run the image, read from the ISA its linked objects
record (``Tag_RISCV_arch``). Even a scalar image may use declared bitmanip or half-float
instructions beyond Spike's default; vector presence is not a prerequisite. Keep the counter
extensions used by the bare-metal harness, and choose the widest declared vector length.

symbols.name: declared_memory
symbols.doc:
``(base, bytes)`` the image states with :data:`DRAM_BASE_SYMBOL` / :data:`DRAM_SPAN_SYMBOL`,
read off its symbol table; ``None`` for an image that states none (the simulator's default span).

symbols.name: _layout
symbols.doc:
Absolute-address memory map for the bare-metal image.

Default (``dram_bytes=None``) is the historical spike map: code@0x80000000, arena@0xC0000000,
weights 256 MB-aligned above it and at least 0x2_0000_0000. spike is told to span it with ``-m``,
so "above the DRAM a real board has" costs nothing there.

On a REAL board it costs everything: an arena at 0xC0000000 and weights at 0x2_0000_0000 are simply
not memory, so the image faults on its first activation. Given ``dram_bytes`` the map is packed
inside ``[dram_base, dram_base + dram_bytes)`` instead — code first, then the weights blob, then the
arena taking the rest — and it FAILS CLOSED if the model does not fit rather than emitting an image
that addresses memory the chip does not have.

symbols.name: _supplemental_object_digest
symbols.doc: Identity of actual linked device/matrix bytes, independent of work paths.

symbols.name: _model_memory_reservations
symbols.doc: Recover the linked stack and the allocator extent compiled by this builder.

symbols.name: build
symbols.doc:
Build a whole-model bare-metal ELF and return its paths, memory and identity.

Lowering arguments retain the ``zephyr_model.build_app`` defaults. The
selected compiler supplies the index width. ``int8_compute`` selects W8A8;
``features``, ``rvv_schedule`` and ``cflags_override`` select preparation and
codegen, and ``vlen`` binds the image's minimum vector length. With no
preparation selection, the original module is lowered directly.

``host_math_policy`` defaults to native. Explicit ``expf_via_double`` changes
returned precision and needs caller numerical qualification; errno and FP
exceptions are not preserved. ``math_archive_symbols`` requests byte-pinned
actual-link supplier traces, not source-call or numerical qualification.

``output_dump_cap`` bounds post-timing raw first-output values;
``output_sha256`` hashes all first-output f32 little-endian bytes after timing.
``full_readback`` selects the complete typed multi-output transport.
``op_profile`` emits top-level operation IDs/ticks/hits using ``mcycle``;
compare its instrumentation separately from unprofiled execution.

``execution_memory_map`` binds a provider-decoded map to execution identity.
Actual ELF, stack, allocator and declared absolute external buffers must fit.
It infers neither map facts from simulator backing size nor peak demand,
aliases or lifetime reuse. No selection leaves emitted bytes unchanged.
``stack_bytes`` reserves each hart's stack; model-dependent alloca must fit.

Default host vector scheduling requires declared floating-vector ISA support.
``host_vectorize`` or an explicit schedule can override this, including LLVM
vector scalarization. Separate device preparation does not imply RVV support.
``host_llvm_transform`` selects a late legalizer with immutable source and
private output directory. Its selected bytes enter the normal build identity.
``host_llvm_transform_chain`` adds ordered checked stages before that hook;
missing promised stages refuse, and no chain preserves the original hook.

``host_provider_builder`` links separately pinned mixed host/provider objects
with source/model identity, compilation and typed symbol checks independent
of a device catalog. ``shared_source_lowerings`` selects checked row,
pointwise or dense discovery and linking; the row-only option remains.
Unsupported source retains its route; explicit hooks cannot be replaced.
``prepared_model_transform`` runs after preparation and before profiling on
an immutable private snapshot. Entry types and selected bytes enter the
recipe; semantic, effect and provider proofs remain caller obligations.
``masked_contraction_effects`` forwards explicit nontrapping/unobserved-FP-flag
permission only with the caller's separate feature and schedule selection.

``console="htif"`` needs host tohost service; UART uses SDK-provided clock and
device facts. ``chip_freq_hz=None`` preserves reset clock. ``matrix`` selects
one routing for rewriting and shim objects; ``matrix_scalar_tile`` diagnoses
packing/ABI with scalar instructions and does not qualify a device datapath.

symbols.name: run
symbols.doc:
Run the ELF on spike; parse the HTIF output. Returns {outputs, metrics, console}.

``mem_bytes`` must cover 0x80000000 .. weights_base + weights size (use the value
returned by :func:`build`).

``vlen`` MUST match the vector length the image was BUILT for, and this is not a preference.
``-march=...zvl<N>b`` makes the compiler emit scalable-vector spill slots whose addresses are computed
from ``vlenb`` READ AT RUN TIME (`csrr a1, vlenb` then a shift and an add). If the simulator reports a
