different ``vlenb``, every such slot lands at the wrong offset -- MEASURED on deepjscc int8: a
``vs1r.v`` spill computed as ``sp + 328 + 16*vlenb + 2384`` is 256 bytes off between VLEN 128 and 256,
and at the wrong length it writes over the memref descriptors sitting nearby.
The bare ``rv64gcv`` in the default ISA string is VLEN=128, so an image built with ``vlen=256`` and run
without this argument was silently running at half the declared width; matching them took the same
model 602k copies further to 2.37M. Pass the ``vlen`` you passed to :func:`build`, or read it back from
that call's result.

symbols.name: run_raw
symbols.doc:
Run the ELF on the plain functional simulator and return its stdout BYTES, unparsed.

The full-readback console (:mod:`merlin.runtime.whole_model_readback`) carries raw payload bytes,
which a text decode would replace; this is :func:`run` without the decode. A state the image
declares (its DRAM span) wins over ``mem_bytes``.

symbols.name: parse_console
symbols.doc: Parse a bounded output prefix; caller owns process and hardware provenance.

symbols.name: build_and_run
symbols.doc:
Build + run + (optionally) gate against a reference array. Returns the run dict
plus ``rel``/``cos``/``ok`` vs the reference. spike memory is sized automatically.

source_files.module_doc:
Explicit source-bound host/provider objects for the ordinary model link.

Device catalogs retain their own closed-object contract. This separate seam
checks imported compilation identities and typed function boundaries, records
ordered linking, and closes every required symbol in the final image. It grants
no numerical, effect, target capability or source-fallback permission.

symbols.name: _function_abis
symbols.doc:
Read canonical LLVM function headers using typed tokens, never names.

Accept only the simple C scalar/pointer ABI used by ranked descriptor and
primitive calls. Aggregate, byval/sret, address-space, non-C conventions and
unknown ABI attributes refuse rather than guessing a function type.

symbols.name: read_host_function_abi
symbols.doc: Read one explicitly named boundary from immutable companion LLVM.

symbols.name: prepare_model_host_provider
symbols.doc: Bind ordinary model artifacts and observed compilation to the provider.

symbols.name: prepare_host_provider
symbols.doc: Invoke an explicit builder and validate every imported boundary and pin.

symbols.name: close_host_provider
symbols.doc: Recheck immutable imports and final ordered object/symbol resolution.

symbols.name: revalidate_host_provider
symbols.doc: Reopen one completed provider through the read-only batch boundary.

symbols.name: revalidate_host_providers
symbols.doc:
Reopen original completed records with one hash per exact path per batch.

The caller retains the producer's original records and excludes concurrent
writes during this callback-free boundary. This is not an atomic filesystem
snapshot. Each new call reopens all files; no identity survives the batch.
Records are frozen before checking and must remain unchanged through return.
``max_records`` bounds the number of original records before any snapshots
or file reads. No ABI, numerical, effect or execution qualification is granted.

source_files.module_doc:
Check counted-schedule integer intermediates without target loading or emission.

The same conservative interval check serves shared verification and C codegen.
It never expands dynamic iterations and grants no target address/window or
completion semantics. Unsupported expressions remain a barrier.

symbols.name: IntegerDomainError
symbols.doc: A selected signed index domain cannot represent every intermediate.

symbols.name: check_integer_domain
symbols.doc: Conservative bounds for every emitted integer intermediate, without expansion.

source_files.module_doc:
Native finite-domain allocation with an independent witness checker.

Z3 solves Merlin's generated placement formula. The checker below evaluates
the selected graph and storage geometry directly without reusing the formula.
An UNSAT result applies only to one candidate, order and bounded model.

symbols.name: topological_orders
symbols.doc: Enumerate bounded legal instruction orders after a low-pressure first order.

symbols.name: instruction_schedule
symbols.doc: Issue serially until target timing has a reviewed overlap contract.

symbols.name: _qualified_in_place_pair
symbols.doc: Permit exact reuse only for a declared, last-use produced operand.

symbols.name: interference_edges
symbols.doc: Canonical storage-conflict edges; order affects only this part of our formula.

symbols.name: check_assignment
symbols.doc: Recompute original geometry/lifetimes without consulting Z3 expressions.

symbols.name: may_prune_interference
symbols.doc: Only a same-base UNSAT graph's supergraph inherits the contradiction.

source_files.module_doc: Shared explicit allocation geometry and graph records, without solver imports.

symbols.name: Reservation
symbols.doc:
Unavailable physical interval, in the bank's explicit address unit.

Reservations last for the entire candidate, across every typed view of the
backing store. Shorter lifetimes need a qualified temporal model.

source_files.module_doc:
Explicit source-bound linked-artifact checks before simulator dispatch.

This transport validates unchanged artifact/report bytes and callback ownership.
Its caller supplies the independently evaluated policy. It grants no physical,
instruction-effect, numerical or timing authority and never resolves a backend.

symbols.name: _receipt
symbols.doc: Retain custody references, never copy a prerequisite's protected findings.

source_files.module_doc: Target-independent xDSL transformations with explicit verification handoff.
Callable structural analysis of actual xDSL IR, independent of target policies.
Scoped structural liveness, bounded pressure accounting and dependency edges.
Conservative aliases/effects; no instruction-name interpretation or guessed widths.
Immutable structural analysis facts, with stable identities from actual IR.

symbols.name: IRIndex
symbols.doc: Linear-size indexing; values retain no identity from another revision.

source_files.module_doc: Structural change identities, not proof receipts or candidate assertions.

symbols.name: ir_text
symbols.doc: Generic printing retains attributes, properties and all SSA dependencies.

symbols.name: ir_digest
calls: hashlib.sha256((op if isinstance(op, str) else ir_text(op)).encode()).hexdigest

symbols.name: parse_ir
symbols.doc: Parse the common domain, retaining opaque OOT operations conservatively.

source_files.module_doc:
Public transport for host-owned transformations and preservation checks.

Clients supply actual IR only. Semantics, coverage, proof tools and acceptance
remain with the original host broker; returned summaries create no authority.

symbols.name: _requester_identity
symbols.doc: The existing original broker compares process leases within one namespace.

symbols.name: apply_transform
symbols.doc: Apply admitted common passes; receipt summaries are descriptive only.

symbols.name: check_transform
symbols.doc: Check an actual rewrite under the frozen host's semantic and proof policy.

source_files.module_doc: Portable scheduling decision IR shared with standalone target compilers.

symbols.name: DenseScheduleOp
symbols.doc:
A selected contraction block, with explicit byte and command bounds.

This records a compile-time choice and executes no command. The target
adapter verifies its realization before emitting this decision.

symbols.name: dense_schedule_op
symbols.doc: Materialize a checked decision without importing a particular planner copy.

symbols.name: _trace_attributes
symbols.doc:
Accept only typed capture attribution; never use its values for legality.

These existing frontend fields name taxonomy, original dtype or source
ancestry. They remain on the exact source. Placement, dispatch, numerical
policy and unknown ``prov.*`` fields are deliberately outside this reader.

symbols.name: recognize_signed_integer_matmul
symbols.doc:
Read exact tensor matmul maps and signed modular multiply/add semantics.

This establishes the scalar recurrence, not zero initialization, ownership,
physical layout, target support or a numerical/qualification receipt.

symbols.name: static_zero_integer_matmul_geometry
symbols.doc:
Read the exact initialized integer dot and its complete static geometry.

This proves the initialized zero value, not physical freshness or ownership.
It establishes no target, packing, effect, numerical admission or execution
capability. The original source is never rewritten.

symbols.name: validate_singleton_projection_map
symbols.doc: Require an ascending dimension projection or zero at a singleton input axis.

symbols.name: checked_static_linalg_shell
symbols.doc: Check the common typed tensor/map shell; never admit a scalar body here.

source_files.module_doc:
Bounded contraction blocking from explicit storage and emission constraints.

This module uses only the standard library so standalone compilers can carry
an exact, versioned copy. Instruction encoding, layouts, effects and numerical
legality belong to the caller. Counts describe requests, never device cycles.

symbols.name: DenseProblem
symbols.doc: Logical contraction and the target's explicit primitive tile representation.

symbols.name: DenseResources
symbols.doc:
Available bytes after reservations, plus the emitter's supported block domain.

Capacities may describe a single usable bank rather than an entire memory.
Shared backings and other live allocations must be accounted for by the
adapter before constructing this view. It creates no asynchronous proof.

symbols.name: DenseBlock
symbols.doc: One legal geometric candidate; target instruction legality is checked separately.

symbols.name: DenseEmission
symbols.doc:
Observations reconstructed by an adapter from its emitted operations.

Load/store counts include loop multiplicities; static commands count each
instruction site once. High-water marks are exclusive byte offsets relative
to the assigned operand and accumulator regions, after decoding addresses.
These observations do not prove aliases, completion or numerical semantics.

symbols.name: verify_dense_emission
symbols.doc:
Require selected reuse and storage bounds to survive target emission.

The adapter must inspect the actual operation stream, including loop bounds
and memory addresses. Copying the planned counts into this report supplies
no evidence. Instruction decoding and physical legality remain target-owned.
A target's price may be a conservative static upper bound.

symbols.name: dense_blocks
symbols.doc:
Enumerate bounded M/N choices without expanding tensors or dynamic loops.

One largest resource-legal K panel is considered for each M/N choice. An
optional physical ``k_limit(bm, bn)`` narrows the logical byte bound for
separate stores, row padding or reserved windows; zero declines that M/N.
The callback supplies a capacity limit, not a performance estimate. This
initial family preserves increasing K per output and holds the complete
output block in private accumulators. Other dataflows need other families.

symbols.name: choose_dense_block
symbols.doc:
Choose a resource-legal candidate priced by its actual target emitter.

``None`` from ``price`` declines a candidate; zero is a valid count. A zero
budget admits only a zero-command candidate. No result asks the caller to
keep its existing legal streaming/loop path. This function emits no code.

symbols.name: DenseGroupChoice
symbols.doc: Full-K shared-LHS choice, over the existing per-member dense blocks.

symbols.name: choose_dense_group
symbols.doc:
Intersect existing block candidates under one finite combined budget.

All members keep the same complete LHS reduction resident. Their RHS and
accumulator windows are separate. This does not grant retention, output
aliasing, instruction semantics or member-interleaving permissions.

source_files.module_doc:
Bounded tensor-level row batching of exact common-RHS integer dots.

Choices use current scalar semantics and immutable tensor coordinates. No
instruction, retention, physical-layout, execution or profitability law is
inferred. Ordinary callers must independently qualify actual emitted products.

symbols.name: _groups
symbols.doc: Read the original source only; no references or candidate costs are used.
calls: partitions.setdefault((operation.parent, k, n, dtypes, root, rhs), []).append

symbols.name: _emit
symbols.doc: Emit actual matmul inputs and exact slices; no copy/concat is introduced.

symbols.name: plan_source_dense_row_batching
symbols.doc: Clone a bounded source candidate, retaining the original on no match.

source_files.module_doc:
Reconstruct row-batched integer contractions from actual source IR.

This checks tensor values and complete unchanged SSA/effect order. It grants no
physical view, retained-load, target execution, allocation or cost authority.

symbols.name: RowBatchingUnavailable
symbols.doc: An original source is outside the bounded mathematical batching domain.

symbols.name: boundary_attributes
symbols.doc: Dispatch attribution survives unchanged; it never selects a batch.

symbols.name: matrix_view
symbols.doc: Read dense matrices or the existing checked rank-three view chain.

symbols.name: rhs_identity
symbols.doc: Exact root, coordinates, permutation, element type and logical shape.

symbols.name: transpose_value
symbols.doc: Read a registered transpose, retaining all its boundary attribution.

symbols.name: _positive_division
symbols.doc: An unchanged integer floor division by a positive literal is total.

symbols.name: safe_span
symbols.doc: Moving total tensor dot arithmetic must not cross unknown effects.

symbols.name: supported_scope
symbols.doc: The first slice has no enclosing loop, lifecycle or unknown ABI contract.

symbols.name: _batch
symbols.doc: Recognize actual emitted prefix and exact output partition, no plan.

symbols.name: verify_dense_row_batching
symbols.doc: Inspect actual grouped domains and every untouched operation/SSA use.

source_files.module_doc: Ordered loop segmentation with constant-size generated IR.

symbols.name: iter_segments
symbols.doc: Lazy execution/reference utility; compiler emission never enumerates this.

symbols.name: segment_loops
symbols.doc:
Strip-mine loops by their original nesting depth, retaining exact order.

Every iter_arg is forwarded through the inner and outer yields. Thus ordered
reductions retain the original accumulator after each element, including
wrapping arithmetic. Arbitrary body effects remain in their original order.
Negative/dynamic bounds and non-index induction types are left unchanged.
Requested static loops whose generated index arithmetic would overflow refuse.

symbols.name: ordered_loop_obligation
symbols.doc: The numerical projection consumed by a parameterized partition theorem.

source_files.module_doc: Conservative scalar-ring and statically known view normalization.

symbols.name: normalize_shapes
symbols.doc:
Eliminate identical memref casts and materialize static dimensions.

No reinterpretation, guessed strides, dynamic-to-static assumptions or
element enumeration. The identity cast also applies to contiguous views
presented through an already identical memref descriptor.

symbols.name: simplify_integers
symbols.doc:
Fold scalar wrapping integers and neutral operands, without poison flags.

Index arithmetic, tensors, floating arithmetic and nsw/nuw operations are
deliberately excluded. Constants are canonicalized modulo the declared
bit width; reductions are never reassociated.

source_files.module_doc: Common callable transformations; verification authority belongs to the host.

symbols.name: apply_common_pipeline
symbols.doc:
Transform a private clone; dispatch every covered change to verification.

``verifier`` is supplied by the host's trusted broker. This API creates no
formal receipts and cannot turn a callback return value into proof authority.
The broker must supply live checker completion. Without
that hook, only explicit ``plan_only`` invocations can produce changed IR.
No callback, successful numerical test or structural certificate proves a
transformation by itself.

source_files.module_doc:
Bounded semantic branch selection over the existing pass session.

Policies are compiler choices, not proofs or hardware qualification. Facts must
come from current IR and selected contracts. They contain no workload identities,
benchmark scores or capsule names. Registered actions retain their original host
verification obligations; target lowering stays in the target adapter.

A compact counted-loop compiler can register its existing compact-IR actions.
This selector does not expand loops or route them through finite schedule IR.

symbols.name: registry_metadata
symbols.doc: Expose only declared pass contracts; no invented knobs or applicability.

symbols.name: execute_policy
symbols.doc:
Run one selected path through the native manager and consume its output.

Use a fresh private session for each bounded candidate variant. There is no
retry after a partially mutating failure, and no fallback to stale artifacts.
Register verified common transforms, schedule compilation or compact target
lowering adapters as appropriate; this function supplies none of their proof
or execution authority. The final pass must produce the requested output on
the current IR, so selected transformations are on the emission path.

symbols.name: VariantEvaluation
symbols.doc: One completed machine-search alternative; compilation is not qualification.

symbols.name: evaluate_variants
symbols.doc:
Yield every applicable explicit variant on a fresh private IR.

This is deterministic compiler search, with no LLM, simulator or implicit
performance model. Variants may select different registered pass orders or
separately registered parameterizations. Each yielded result is immediately
available to the caller's rolling execution queue. Unsupported/unknown guards
never become permissions; failed alternatives discard their partial IR and
cannot contaminate later alternatives. No automatic fallback or ranking is
inferred from a compilation result.

``facts(session)`` derives the existing typed facts for the current clone.
Ordinary xDSL modules use their native clone/verification. Alternate counted
IR must supply clone, fingerprint and verify_ir adapters without flattening
loops. Host transform verification and independent execution obligations are
unchanged. The source must remain immutable while this iterator is consumed.

An explicit ``prefix`` executes shared preparation once before branching.
Its transformed IR is cloned, while all prefix analyses are discarded: each
branch must derive its own current facts and any pass prerequisites. This is
invocation-local preparation, not a persistent cache or reusable proof. Only
preparation legal for every alternative belongs in the unconditional prefix.

source_files.module_doc:
Shared pass state and invalidation, independent of transform execution brokers.

These are source/context custody checks, not proof or execution authority.
The structured transform driver reexports the same types and owns its verifier.

symbols.name: PipelineContext
symbols.doc:
Identities of the selected contracts, not declarations of hardware support.

Missing identities remain unknown. They cannot authorize an optimization
requiring hardware, numerical or execution facts. Hosts supply their own
reviewed contracts; an author cannot obtain permissions by naming a digest.

symbols.name: PassSpec
symbols.doc: Small execution contract shared by structured and ordinary model passes.

symbols.name: validate_pass_order
symbols.doc: Reject explicit ordering errors before executing any transformation.

symbols.name: PipelineSession
symbols.doc:
Current-IR analysis custody and bounded repair, without proof authority.

Consumers still validate their analyses independently. Fingerprints detect
out-of-band mutations, including changes made without this runner. A pass
failure poisons this private session; its partially rewritten IR cannot be
consumed or reported as a successful compilation.

source_files.module_doc: IR-derived storage lifetimes and conservative sequential effect dependencies.

symbols.name: _full_write_initializer
symbols.doc: Recognize one complete rectangular write, without enumerating coordinates.

symbols.name: plan_storage
symbols.doc:
Plan identical-type reuse in direct allocation scopes.

Only static contiguous byte-addressable scalar integer buffers with a
recognized complete initialization and explicit deallocation are eligible.
Escapes, aliases, dynamic layouts and asynchronous lifetimes remain unknown.
Distinct memref allocations are intrinsically disjoint; caller input alias
assertions are neither needed nor accepted.

symbols.name: reuse_storage
symbols.doc: Apply a freshly recomputed plan, never trust a caller's interval claims.

symbols.name: plan_dependencies
symbols.doc:
SSA edges plus an ordered chain of all side-effecting operations.

This initial sequential planner permits independent pure scalar work to
move, while conservatively ordering even read/read effects and all unknown
device/configuration operations. It does not infer missing OOT effects.

symbols.name: apply_order
symbols.doc: Apply a permutation only after deriving dependencies from the current IR.

source_files.module_doc:
Guarded upstream xDSL scalar CSE/DCE and loop-invariant motion.

All transformed operations are total, effect-free, fixed-width scalar integer
operations. Unknown effects, memory accesses, regions, index arithmetic, poison
flags and unmodeled metadata remain unchanged. Hardware policies are absent.

symbols.name: eligible_scalar_operation
symbols.doc: Closed total arithmetic domain; operation traits alone do not admit OOT code.

symbols.name: _ScalarCSE
symbols.doc: Use upstream equivalence, dominance scopes and rewriting with a narrower domain.

symbols.name: eliminate_scalar_redundancy
symbols.doc:
Mutate admitted scalar operations, retaining opaque consumers and all effects.

Upstream CSE includes leaf DCE. A guarded upstream liveness fixpoint then
deletes complete dead scalar chains. Every other operation is a liveness
root, including unreachable-block effects and terminators. No CFG is changed.
Space depends on IR size, not tensor dimensions or iteration counts.

symbols.name: hoist_scalar_invariants
symbols.doc:
Hoist total scalar expressions with operands outside the immediate loop.

Upstream ownership and speculation analysis provide the movement preconditions.
Only direct-body admitted operations are moved; unknown region semantics are
not crossed. Zero-trip and dynamic loops are safe because this domain has no
trapping, poison-producing or observable operations. Loop-carried values and
induction variables remain variant. Chained invariants move in SSA order.

source_files.module_doc:
Bounded, explicitly permitted integer source recomputation candidates.

The original source stays unchanged. A returned proposal is legal under its
original host permissions, not a performance decision, admission or target
qualification. Existing layout/storage passes retain their original guards.

symbols.name: RecomputationPermissions
symbols.doc: Original host premises; identifiers and records grant no permission.

symbols.name: RecomputationBudgets
symbols.doc:
Construction counts include the full cloned module, not net IR growth.

Logical evaluations count all scalar operations, including constants.
These finite ceilings never establish repeatability or hardware support.

symbols.name: implementation_paths
symbols.doc: Direct semantic owners; this is not arbitrary transitive qualification.

symbols.name: plan_source_recomputation
symbols.doc:
Return the first bounded legal candidate, or retain the original with None.

The caller supplies original permissions before discovery. No observed
outputs, baseline compile, cost estimate or captured identity selects it.

source_files.module_doc:
Independent full-module correspondence for bounded source recomputation.

This does not relax the layout pass's prohibition on extra arithmetic. The
original host must separately permit repeated evaluation and storage removal.
No target execution, allocation removal or performance qualification is issued.

symbols.name: _blocks
symbols.doc: Stable structural paths, independent of SSA names and object identity.

symbols.name: _composed_graph
symbols.doc:
Reconstruct exact ordered applications and shared constant captures.

Scalar captures remain original dominating constants; they are never moved
into an element loop or evaluated twice merely to simplify correspondence.

symbols.name: _skeleton
symbols.doc: Check every other op, metadata, region and complete operand wiring.

symbols.name: verify_source_recomputation
symbols.doc:
Reconstruct a sole fan-out rewrite without trusting emitter reports.

Both modules must be independently parsed/verified current IR. Shape,
ordered modular operations, captures, complete outputs and opaque effect
epochs are reconstructed; hashes alone never establish repeated work.

source_files.module_doc:
Adapt actual sequential xDSL SSA to the existing checked generic allocator.

The result is a resource assignment in an explicitly supplied representation,
not an instruction encoding, hardware timing estimate or numerical proof.
Annotation validation recomputes graph/lifetimes and independently checks the
actual recorded addresses; it never accepts a solver status string alone.

symbols.name: allocate_instruction_resources
symbols.doc:
Solve one source-order allocation, never infer banks/units from op names.

Extents are supplied by the admitted physical representation; logical bytes
alone cannot qualify them. Effect operands are conservatively retained to
scope completion. This sequential epoch model makes no latency/overlap claim.

symbols.name: validate_allocated_ir
symbols.doc: Check actual emitted assignment independently of the solver and plan object.

source_files.module_doc:
Schedule closed source normalization islands one complete row at a time.

The original maximum, subtraction, exponential, sum and division regions are
retained, including their scalar operation order, attributes and initializers.
Only independent row fibers are interchanged. Source masks and nonfinite values
remain ordinary source values; no finite-domain approximation is introduced.
Unknown effects, layouts, observers, indexing and source algorithms retain the
original route. Ordinary serial host lowering consumes this transformation.

symbols.name: row_input_projection
symbols.doc: Interpret a static axis projection/broadcast; never flatten unknown maps.

symbols.name: match_row_normalization
symbols.doc: Recognize from current typed source dataflow; provenance never selects it.

symbols.name: emit_row_normalization
symbols.doc: Emit ordinary tensor/SCF/linalg; upstream still owns CPU bufferization.

symbols.name: ordered_contraction
symbols.doc:
Recognize a typed ordered multiply/add boundary for the cost policy.

This classifies unchanged consumers/producers; it neither lowers a
contraction nor grants a target primitive or reassociation capability.

symbols.name: row_state_cost_reason
symbols.doc: Conservative unknown-cost policy, including existing fusion boundaries.

symbols.name: fuse_row_normalizations
symbols.doc:
Automatically row-schedule admitted closed source islands on a private IR.

Standard pure tensor/scalar semantics retain their values, initializers and
per-row reduction order. No approximation, finite-domain assumption, target
capability or runtime persistence is inferred. Unmatched/observed/effectful
islands retain their original route. The returned facts describe source IR;
actual physical allocation and execution need independent observation.

source_files.module_doc:
Check actual row-local source replay and restore the complete surrounding IR.

No selected row plan proves itself: original scalar regions, initializer data,
actual loop bounds, slices, recurrence and local producer/consumer SSA are
checked separately. Inverting checked islands must reconstruct the entire
original module, including every unselected operation and escaping observation.
This is a structural semantic check, not a Lean or machine-code receipt.

symbols.name: verify_row_normalization_record
symbols.doc: Reconstruct one actual complete-row wrapper and its original source DAG.

symbols.name: verify_row_normalizations
symbols.doc: Check actual islands; invert them and compare the entire source module.

source_files.module_doc:
Actual-operation witnesses for conservative scalar reuse and invariant motion.

These records carry no proof authority. Their replay validator is part of the
explicit structural-checker trusted computing base, separately from Lean lemmas.

symbols.name: validate_scalar_change
symbols.doc: Reopen and replay the admitted mechanism against the actual complete IR.

source_files.module_doc:
Bounded ordered unrolling; code growth follows an explicit compiler budget.

This mechanism selects no profitable factor. It preserves each original body
evaluation, including its effects and loop-carried state, in its original order.

symbols.name: unroll_ordered_loops
symbols.doc:
Fully inline small loops or partially unroll a bounded bulk plus exact tail.

Factors index original nesting depth. Dynamic/negative bounds and unsupported
metadata remain unchanged. Requested arithmetic overflow or code growth
refuses the transformation. No tensor elements or trip-count-sized structures
are allocated. Callers should transform a private clone for transactional use.

symbols.name: validate_unrolled_change
symbols.doc:
Bind actual emitted instructions, IV substitutions and state to the source.

Trusted structural replay is explicit; arithmetic/fold obligations are checked
by the independent host Lean route, not by this correspondence validator.

source_files.module_doc:
Recognize actual generated structure before issuing abstract proof obligations.

This is a structural guard, never an equivalence proof receipt. In particular,
the loop recognizer checks actual IV substitution, carried state, tail bounds,
body preservation and unrelated surrounding IR independently of code emission.

symbols.name: validate_change
symbols.doc: Reject stale identities, forged witnesses or different actual rewrites.

source_files.module_doc:
Conditional packing ownership and footprint in the actual compiled host LLVM.

The stock importer and existing CFG/SCC analyses own syntax and control flow.
This closed checker follows allocation-relative address expressions, original
ranked call descriptors and complete borrowed-call premises. It neither moves
storage nor qualifies a runtime, provider implementation or native compiler.

symbols.name: PackingAllocationEffects
symbols.doc:
Explicit original runtime premises, never inferred from symbol spellings.

Fresh private allocation means a disjoint contiguous object of the complete
requested byte extent. Success includes non-null, representable storage.
The separately selected pointer width must match every address conversion.
Releases are possible only through the selected deallocator. These are
original qualification premises; this record proves none of them.

symbols.name: PackingStorageRequest
symbols.doc: One original island's use roster and logical-payload budget.

symbols.name: _alignment
symbols.doc: Match complete round-up from this exact raw pointer, not just low bits.

symbols.name: verify_packing_storage
symbols.doc:
Prove finite distinct packing ownership under original runtime/ABI effects.

The budget is logical activation payload, not total host RAM. Gather-value
correctness and all unrelated memory-access bounds remain separate source,
compiler and execution obligations.

symbols.name: verify_packing_storage_batch
symbols.doc:
Check one actual entry once, retaining each island's independent budget.

Common roots count once in the union and once in every participating island.
Projection cannot transfer spare budget between islands. Source-domain
coverage remains the caller's separate original-source obligation.

symbols.name: inspect_packing_storage_batch
symbols.doc: Import and analyze the common actual entry once for all original islands.

source_files.module_doc:
Source-bound Lean obligations for the actual checked SSA resource annotation.

The projection and source-to-epoch interpretation are trusted. No saved status,
solver result or projection object issues accepted evidence. Hardware sizes,
units, effects and qualified overwrite meanings remain independent obligations.

symbols.name: resource_semantic_identity
symbols.doc: Bind the trusted projector/checker and mathematical model source bytes.

symbols.name: _overwrite
symbols.doc: Recover the actual declared last-use exception, not a solver permission.

symbols.name: project_resource_geometry
symbols.doc:
Validate and project actual assignments, including all result-free events.

Bounds count IR values/relations, never tensor elements or address units.
No placement solver is run. A host checker must call this function freshly
and bind its identities; accepting a caller-supplied object is insufficient.

symbols.name: lean_resource_query
symbols.doc: Render one kernel-checkable conjunction; this does not issue a receipt.

scope: All direct Python modules in transforms and compile/scheduling, all reference-document code_refs, plus explicitly followed connected-region and host-arithmetic dependencies; not a transitive whole-repository inventory
